literature.headline_zh: 登革病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期登革病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 根据 GMT 比率测量,V181 对 DENV-1 和 DENV-2 诱导 免疫应答 不劣于 Butantan-DV,但对 DENV-3 和 DENV-4 不诱导 免疫应答。根据血清转化率确定所有 DENV 血清型的非劣效性。大多数参与者产生了三价或四价中和抗体反应,每种 DENV 血清型均检测到 疫苗 病毒血症。 [10.1093/cid/ciag349]
NS1Ag-RDT 的敏感性为 95.36%,特异性为 92.74%,与 NS1Ag-ELISA 高度一致。 [10.1128/spectrum.00073-26]

Shela 亚群表现出易感性(>98% 死亡率),而印地语和 Mokowe 亚群表现出耐药性,死亡率 率分别为 47% 和 37.6%。来自印地语的蚊子 (n = 60);莫科韦 (n = 90);和 Shela (n = 130)、n = 14 (23%)、n = 24 (27%) 和 n = 40 (31%) 分别患有登革热 2 中肠感染;n = 12 (20%)、n = 11 (12%) 和 n = 21 (16%) 分别患有播散性感染。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0359810]

NAC组的住院时间明显更短(平均5.01天,标准差1.28 vs 6.12天,标准差1.25;P<.001)。NAC组的AST和ALT水平显著降低(AST:平均154.83 U/L,标准差67.22 vs 184.62 U/L,标准差79.88;P=.02;ALT:平均113.09 U/L,标准差33.31 vs 156.35 U/L,标准差73.66;P=.004)。治疗后血小板计数在NAC组显著升高(中位数31.50 G/L,四分位距19.00-50.15 vs 17.00 G/L,四分位距8.75-36.23;P=.001)。NAC组的血小板计数增加中位数也更大(15.05 G/L,四分位距7.05-26.10 vs 6.95 G/L,四分位距4.22-15.43;P=.001)。研究期间未记录到严重的输注相关不良事件。 [10.2196/97990]
热带地区的大多数大城市以及温带地区越来越多的大城市现在面临着不断变化的虫媒病毒威胁。 [10.1038/s44528-026-00036-z]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: V181 induced a noninferior immune response to Butantan-DV for DENV-1 and DENV-2 but not DENV-3 and DENV-4, as measured using GMT ratios. Noninferiority was established for all DENV serotypes based on seroconversion rates. [10.1093/cid/ciag349]
The NS1Ag-RDT demonstrated a sensitivity of 95.36% and specificity of 92.74%, showing strong agreement with NS1Ag-ELISA. [10.1128/spectrum.00073-26]

The Shela sub-population displayed susceptibility (>98% mortality), whereas the Hindi and Mokowe sub-populations exhibited resistance, with mortality rates of 47% and 37.6%, respectively. [10.1371/journal.pone.0359810]

The NAC group had a significantly shorter hospital stay (mean 5.01, SD 1.28 vs 6.12, SD 1.25 days; P<.001). The AST and ALT levels were significantly lower in the NAC group (AST: mean 154.83, SD 67.22 vs 184.62, SD 79.88 U/L and P=.02; ALT: mean 113.09, SD 33.31 vs 156.35, SD 73.66 U/L and P=.004). [10.2196/97990]
Most large cities in the tropics, and an increasing number in temperate zones, now face a shifting mix of arboviral threats. [10.1038/s44528-026-00036-z]

literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.

news.headline_zh: 登革病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期登革病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 马绍尔群岛、萨摩亚、瓦努阿图、瓦利斯和富图纳群岛报告了登革热 暴发。暴发 已确诊,有实验室确诊病例并正在进行监测。该报告还提到了澳大利亚的麻疹 暴发 和瓦努阿图的百日咳 暴发,但这些并不是分析的主要重点。 [news-5e8b56dde66a4ef5]
据 CIDRAP 报道,一名坦帕妇女死于登革热,这是佛罗里达州病例激增的一部分。 [news-c7628cec31e3b581]
发表在 Parasites & 媒介 上的一项研究发现,地中海白纹伊蚊种群的遗传血统显着影响其传播基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 和 登革病毒 (DENV) 的能力。这一发现基于群体遗传学和实验 媒介 能力测定。研究结果证实了这一事件。 [news-6b2e537ac01953c3]
报告有252例确诊病例的登革热 暴发,但没有具体确认病毒类型(N10)。暴发 与热带风暴伊萨亚斯有关,预计该风暴将加强并带来强降雨和零星雷暴(N10、N13、N15、N16、N17)。 [news-115d132e50fd0c1e]
佛罗里达州的 登革热 暴发 病例已超过 250 例,其中大多数报告在希尔斯伯勒县。该事件已得到当地新闻报道的证实。 [news-78bc794a5ef58326]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Dengue virus news developments.
key_findings_en: Dengue outbreaks were reported in the Marshall Islands, Samoa, Vanuatu, and Wallis and Futuna. The outbreaks are confirmed, with laboratory-confirmed cases and ongoing monitoring. [news-5e8b56dde66a4ef5]
A Tampa woman died from dengue, reported by CIDRAP as part of a surge of cases in Florida. [news-c7628cec31e3b581]

A study published in Parasites & Vectors found that the genetic ancestry of Mediterranean Aedes albopictus populations significantly influences their competence to transmit chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and dengue virus (DENV). This finding was based on population genetics and experimental vector competence assays. [news-6b2e537ac01953c3]

A dengue fever outbreak with 252 confirmed cases was reported, with no specific confirmation of the virus type (N10). The outbreak is linked to Tropical Storm Isaias, which is expected to strengthen and bring heavy rainfall and scattered thunderstorms (N10, N13, N15, N16, N17). [news-115d132e50fd0c1e]
Florida's dengue fever outbreak has surpassed 250 cases, with the majority reported in Hillsborough County. The event is confirmed by local news reports. [news-78bc794a5ef58326]

马绍尔群岛、萨摩亚、瓦努阿图、瓦利斯和富图纳群岛报告了登革热 暴发。暴发 已确诊,有实验室确诊病例并正在进行监测。该报告还提到了澳大利亚的麻疹 暴发 和瓦努阿图的百日咳 暴发,但这些并不是分析的主要重点。
据 CIDRAP 报道,一名坦帕妇女死于登革热,这是佛罗里达州病例激增的一部分。 [news-c7628cec31e3b581]。
发表在 Parasites & 媒介 上的一项研究发现,地中海白纹伊蚊种群的遗传血统显着影响其传播基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 和 登革病毒 (DENV) 的能力。这一发现基于群体遗传学和实验 媒介 能力测定。研究结果证实了这一事件。
报告有252例确诊病例的登革热 暴发,但没有具体确认病毒类型(N10)。暴发 与热带风暴伊萨亚斯有关,预计该风暴将加强并带来强降雨和零星雷暴(N10、N13、N15、N16、N17)。 [news-115d132e50fd0c1e]。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following Dengue virus news developments.

Dengue outbreaks were reported in the Marshall Islands, Samoa, Vanuatu, and Wallis and Futuna. The outbreaks are confirmed, with laboratory-confirmed cases and ongoing monitoring. [news-5e8b56dde66a4ef5].
A Tampa woman died from dengue, reported by CIDRAP as part of a surge of cases in Florida. [news-c7628cec31e3b581].

A study published in Parasites & Vectors found that the genetic ancestry of Mediterranean Aedes albopictus populations significantly influences their competence to transmit chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and dengue virus (DENV).
A dengue fever outbreak with 252 confirmed cases was reported, with no specific confirmation of the virus type (N10).

papers.title: Safety and Immunogenicity of the Live-Attenuated Quadrivalent Dengue Vaccine V181 Compared With Butantan-DV Among Healthy Adults in Brazil: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Phase 2 Trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue is caused by infection with 1 of 4 dengue virus (DENV) serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4). V181 and Butantan-Dengue Vaccine (Butantan-DV) are independently developed, single-dose, quadrivalent dengue vaccines based on the same attenuated parental strains. METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind, active comparator-controlled, multisite, phase 2 trial, we compared the safety and immunogenicity of V181 and Butantan-DV in healthy adults in Brazil. The primary immunogenicity objectives were to compare vaccine-induced neutralizing antibody geometric mean titers (GMTs) and seroconversion rates for DENV-1 to DENV-4 at day 28 postvaccination. The primary and secondary safety objectives, respectively, were to assess vaccine-related serious adverse events and the proportion of participants experiencing solicited adverse events through day 28 postvaccination. RESULTS: Overall, 1364 participants were assigned (1:1) to receive V181 (n = 682) or Butantan-DV (n = 682). At day 28 postvaccination, V181 induced a noninferior immune response to Butantan-DV for DENV-1 and DENV-2 but not DENV-3 and DENV-4, as measured using GMT ratios. Noninferiority was established for all DENV serotypes based on seroconversion rates. Most participants developed a trivalent or tetravalent neutralizing antibody response. Vaccine viremia was detected for each DENV serotype. V181 and Butantan-DV were generally well tolerated. CONCLUSIONS: V181 was immunogenic in adults, and while immunogenicity was noninferior to Butantan-DV for DENV-1 and DENV-2, seroconversion rates were noninferior for DENV-1 to DENV-4. The safety profile of V181 is comparable to that of Butantan-DV and supports its continued evaluation as a single-dose quadrivalent vaccine for dengue prevention. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: NCT05710224.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在比较减毒活四价登革热 疫苗 V181 与布坦坦-DV 在巴西健康成年人中的安全性和免疫原性。登革热是由四种 登革病毒 (DENV) 血清型(DENV-1 至 DENV-4)之一感染引起。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 进行了一项随机、双盲、主动对照、多中心、2 期试验,以比较 V181 和 Butantan-DV 在巴西 1364 名健康成年人中的安全性和免疫原性。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究比较了 疫苗 诱导的中和抗体几何平均滴度 (GMT) 以及疫苗接种后 28 天时 DENV-1 至 DENV-4 的血清转化率。通过评估 疫苗 相关的严重不良事件以及接种后第 28 天经历不良事件的参与者比例来评估安全性。
elements_zh.main_results: 根据 GMT 比率测量,V181 对 DENV-1 和 DENV-2 诱导 免疫应答 不劣于 Butantan-DV,但对 DENV-3 和 DENV-4 不诱导 免疫应答。根据血清转化率确定所有 DENV 血清型的非劣效性。大多数参与者产生了三价或四价中和抗体反应,每种 DENV 血清型均检测到 疫苗 病毒血症。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: V181 的安全性与 Butantan-DV 相当,支持其作为预防登革热的单剂量四价 疫苗 的持续评估。对于 DENV-1 和 DENV-2,V181 的免疫原性不低于 Butantan-DV,对于 DENV-1 和 DENV-4 的血清转化率也不低于。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,V181 是用于预防登革热的 Butantan-DV 的可行替代品,且安全性相当。这支持对 V181 作为单剂量四价 疫苗 的进一步评估。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its design as a phase 2 trial, which may not fully generalize to real-world settings. The sample size is adequate for the primary objectives but may be insufficient for subgroup analyses. The study does not report any concrete limitations that would significantly impact the evidence strength.

papers.title: How climate change affects mosquito-borne infectious disease: The different trajectories of malaria and dengue
papers.abstract: As climate change increases temperatures, additional warmth combines with rainfall and humidity to enhance conditions for mosquito populations to thrive. Greater spread of Anopheles and Aedes vectors increases the risk of transmission of the world’s most prevalent mosquito-borne infectious diseases, malaria and dengue. Yet the impacts of climate drivers on disease transmission are complex: Relationships are nonlinear, effects are seasonal, and there is substantial local variability. Further complexity is added by the many nonclimate factors that influence disease transmission, including movement of people, population growth, immunity levels, land use change, urbanization, control interventions, and quality of health care systems. Here, we explain why, despite climate drivers having broadly similar effects on malaria and dengue transmission parameters, the trajectories of the two diseases differ, with rapid growth in dengue but long-term decline in malaria.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines how climate change affects mosquito-borne infectious diseases, specifically focusing on dengue virus and dengue disease. It explores the complex interactions between climate drivers and disease transmission, highlighting the differing trajectories of malaria and dengue.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of climate change impacts on mosquito-borne diseases, with a focus on dengue. It discusses the role of temperature, rainfall, and humidity in enhancing mosquito populations and the spread of diseases. The review also outlines the influence of nonclimate factors on disease transmission.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that climate change has broadly similar effects on malaria and dengue transmission parameters, but the trajectories of the two diseases differ. Dengue is experiencing rapid growth, while malaria is showing a long-term decline, despite shared environmental influences.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges that the impacts of climate drivers on disease transmission are complex, with nonlinear relationships, seasonal effects, and substantial local variability. It also highlights the influence of nonclimate factors, which can obscure or modify climate-related trends, creating evidence gaps.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests the need for targeted research and surveillance on dengue virus dynamics, particularly in regions experiencing climate change. It emphasizes the importance of integrating climate data with public health strategies to address the growing threat of dengue.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores how climate change influences mosquito-borne diseases, with a focus on dengue virus. It highlights that while climate factors like temperature, rainfall, and humidity enhance mosquito populations and disease transmission, the effects on malaria and dengue differ significantly. Dengue is showing rapid growth, whereas malaria is declining over time. The review underscores the complexity of climate-disease interactions, noting nonlinear relationships, seasonal effects, and local variability. It also identifies nonclimate factors such as population movement, immunity levels, and urbanization as important modifiers of these trends. The findings suggest the need for integrated research and surveillance strategies to address the evolving public health challenges posed by dengue in a changing climate.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,气候变化对疟疾和登革热 传播 参数的影响大致相似,但两种疾病的发展轨迹不同。尽管受到共同的环境影响,登革热正在快速增长,而疟疾则呈现长期下降趋势。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述承认,气候驱动因素对疾病的影响是复杂的,具有非线性关系、季节性影响和显着的局部变异性。它还强调了非气候因素的影响,这些因素可能掩盖或改变与气候相关的趋势,从而造成证据差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查表明需要对 监测 动态进行有针对性的研究和 监测,特别是在经历气候变化的地区。它强调了将气候数据与公共卫生战略相结合以应对日益严重的登革热威胁的重要性。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines how climate change affects mosquito-borne infectious diseases, specifically focusing on dengue virus and dengue disease. It explores the complex interactions between climate drivers and disease transmission, highlighting the differing trajectories of malaria and dengue.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of climate change impacts on mosquito-borne diseases, with a focus on dengue. It discusses the role of temperature, rainfall, and humidity in enhancing mosquito populations and the spread of diseases. The review also outlines the influence of nonclimate factors on disease transmission.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that climate change has broadly similar effects on malaria and dengue transmission parameters, but the trajectories of the two diseases differ. Dengue is experiencing rapid growth, while malaria is showing a long-term decline, despite shared environmental influences.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges that the impacts of climate drivers on disease transmission are complex, with nonlinear relationships, seasonal effects, and substantial local variability. It also highlights the influence of nonclimate factors, which can obscure or modify climate-related trends, creating evidence gaps.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests the need for targeted research and surveillance on dengue virus dynamics, particularly in regions experiencing climate change. It emphasizes the importance of integrating climate data with public health strategies to address the growing threat of dengue.

papers.title_zh: 气候变化如何影响蚊媒传染病:疟疾和登革热的不同轨迹
papers.source_body_en: As climate change increases temperatures, additional warmth combines with rainfall and humidity to enhance conditions for mosquito populations to thrive. Greater spread of Anopheles and Aedes vectors increases the risk of transmission of the world’s most prevalent mosquito-borne infectious diseases, malaria and dengue. Yet the impacts of climate drivers on disease transmission are complex: Relationships are nonlinear, effects are seasonal, and there is substantial local variability. Further complexity is added by the many nonclimate factors that influence disease transmission, including movement of people, population growth, immunity levels, land use change, urbanization, control interventions, and quality of health care systems. Here, we explain why, despite climate drivers having broadly similar effects on malaria and dengue transmission parameters, the trajectories of the two diseases differ, with rapid growth in dengue but long-term decline in malaria.

papers.title: A comparative analysis of rapid diagnostic tests and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays for dengue diagnosis: a retrospective study in a tertiary care hospital in India
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Dengue fever remains a major public health concern in India, where rapid and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective patient care and outbreak control. While enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) serves as the diagnostic standard, NS1 antigen-based rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) offer faster and more accessible alternatives, particularly in resource-limited settings. This retrospective study analyzed 3,488 patient samples tested using both NS1Ag-RDT and NS1Ag-ELISA between January 2023 and December 2024. Using ELISA as the reference standard, the diagnostic accuracy of NS1Ag-based RDT was determined. 1,036 cases were ELISA-positive and 2,452 cases were ELISA-negative; the RDT identified 988 true positives, 2,274 true negatives, 178 false positives, and 48 false negatives. The NS1Ag-RDT demonstrated a sensitivity of 95.36% and specificity of 92.74%, indicating strong agreement with NS1Ag-ELISA. These findings support the utility of NS1Ag-based RDTs as reliable tools for early dengue diagnosis, while highlighting the need for multicentric studies incorporating RT-PCR to further validate diagnostic performance across diverse settings. IMPORTANCE: Dengue virus infection continues to represent a public health burden in endemic regions, where timely and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective patient management and outbreak control. In this context, NS1 antigen-based diagnostic assays play an essential role in routine clinical practice, particularly in resource-limited settings due to limited access to molecular diagnostics. This study provides robust, real-world evidence on the diagnostic performance of NS1 antigen-based rapid diagnostic tests through a large retrospective analysis of 3,488 patient samples collected over a 2-year period at a tertiary care center in India. The findings demonstrate high sensitivity and specificity of NS1Ag-RDTs when compared with NS1Ag-based enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and further highlight seasonal variations in diagnostic accuracy, offering clinically relevant insights that can inform diagnostic strategies during peak transmission periods. This work strengthens the evidence base supporting NS1-based diagnostics in dengue-endemic settings and contributes data of significant relevance to virology-focused research and public health practice.

While enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) serves as the diagnostic standard, NS1 antigen-based rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) offer faster and more accessible alternatives, particularly in resource-limited settings. This retrospective study analyzed 3,488 patient samples tested using both NS1Ag-RDT and NS1Ag-ELISA between January 2023 and December 2024. Using ELISA as the reference standard, the diagnostic accuracy of NS1Ag-based RDT was determined. 1,036 cases were ELISA-positive and 2,452 cases were ELISA-negative; the RDT identified 988 true positives, 2,274 true negatives, 178 false positives, and 48 false negatives. The NS1Ag-RDT demonstrated a sensitivity of 95.36% and specificity of 92.74%, indicating strong agreement with NS1Ag-ELISA. These findings support the utility of NS1Ag-based RDTs as reliable tools for early dengue diagnosis, while highlighting the need for multicentric studies incorporating RT-PCR to further validate diagnostic performance across diverse settings. IMPORTANCE: Dengue virus infection continues to represent a public health burden in endemic regions, where timely and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective patient management and outbreak control. In this context, NS1 antigen-based diagnostic assays play an essential role in routine clinical practice, particularly in resource-limited settings due to limited access to molecular diagnostics. This study provides robust, real-world evidence on the diagnostic performance of NS1 antigen-based rapid diagnostic tests through a large retrospective analysis of 3,488 patient samples collected over a 2-year period at a tertiary care center in India. The findings demonstrate high sensitivity and specificity of NS1Ag-RDTs when compared with NS1Ag-based enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and further highlight seasonal variations in diagnostic accuracy, offering clinically relevant insights that can inform diagnostic strategies during peak transmission periods. This work strengthens the evidence base supporting NS1-based diagnostics in dengue-endemic settings and contributes data of significant relevance to virology-focused research and public health practice.

papers.abstract_zh: 未标记:登革热 仍然是印度的一个主要公共卫生问题,快速而准确的 诊断 对于有效的患者护理和 暴发 控制至关重要。虽然酶联免疫吸附测定 (ELISA) 作为诊断标准,但基于 NS1 抗原的快速诊断测试 (RDT) 提供了更快、更容易获得的替代方案,特别是在资源有限的环境中。这项回顾性研究分析了 2023 年 1 月至 2024 年 12 月期间使用 NS1Ag-RDT 和 NS1Ag-ELISA 检测的 3,488 例患者样本。以 ELISA 作为参考标准,确定了基于 NS1Ag 的 RDT 的诊断准确性。ELISA 阳性 1,036 例,ELISA 阴性 2,452 例;RDT 识别出 988 个真阳性、2,274 个真阴性、178 个假阳性和 48 个假阴性。NS1Ag-RDT 的敏感性为 95.36%,特异性为 92.74%,与 NS1Ag-ELISA 高度一致。这些发现支持基于 NS1Ag 的 RDT 作为早期登革热 诊断 的可靠工具的实用性,同时强调需要结合 RT-PCR 进行多中心研究,以进一步验证不同环境下的诊断性能。重要性:登革病毒 感染仍然是流行地区的公共卫生负担,及时、准确的 诊断 对于有效的患者管理和 暴发 控制至关重要。在这种情况下,基于 NS1 抗原的诊断测定在常规临床实践中发挥着重要作用,特别是在由于分子诊断的机会有限而资源有限的环境中。这项研究通过对印度一家三级护理中心 2 年期间收集的 3,488 名患者样本进行大型回顾性分析,为基于 NS1 抗原的快速诊断测试的诊断性能提供了强有力的真实证据。研究结果表明,与基于 NS1Ag 的酶联免疫吸附测定 (ELISA) 相比,NS1Ag-RDT 具有较高的灵敏度和特异性,并进一步突出了诊断准确性的季节性变化,提供了临床相关的见解,可以为 传播 高峰期的诊断策略提供参考。这项工作加强了支持登革热流行环境中基于 NS1 的诊断的证据基础,并提供了与以病毒学为重点的研究和公共卫生实践密切相关的数据。

papers.title: Intravenous N-Acetylcysteine in Patients With Dengue Fever With Marked Aminotransferase Elevation: Prospective Comparative Study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue fever can lead to significant hepatic involvement and marked aminotransferase elevation and is associated with increased morbidity and prolonged hospitalization. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) has been proposed as a supportive therapy for dengue-induced liver injury. However, prospective comparative evidence from endemic regions such as Vietnam remains limited. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the association between intravenous NAC administration and clinical outcomes (primarily length of hospital stay), as well as the secondary effects of NAC on liver transaminase levels (posttreatment aspartate aminotransferase [AST] and alanine aminotransferase [ALT] and their changes from baseline) and platelet recovery in patients with dengue fever with marked aminotransferase elevation (AST or ALT ≥400 U/L). METHODS: A prospective, nonrandomized comparative study was conducted at the Department of Tropical Diseases, Viet Tiep Hospital, Hai Phong, Vietnam, from June to December 2024. A total of 128 adult patients with laboratory-confirmed dengue fever and marked aminotransferase elevation (AST and/or ALT ≥400 U/L) were enrolled. Treatment allocation was not randomized and was determined by the treating physicians based on aminotransferase elevation and overall clinical condition. Patients received either intravenous NAC (100 mg per kilogram per day) plus standard supportive care (NAC group; n=68) or standard care alone (non-NAC group; n=60). The primary outcome was length of hospital stay. Secondary outcomes included liver transaminase levels and platelet recovery at discharge. RESULTS: Baseline AST, ALT, bilirubin, and international normalized ratio values were broadly comparable between groups, although several clinical and hematological characteristics differed at baseline. The NAC group had a significantly shorter hospital stay (mean 5.01, SD 1.28 vs 6.12, SD 1.25 days; P<.001). The AST and ALT levels were significantly lower in the NAC group (AST: mean 154.83, SD 67.22 vs 184.62, SD 79.88 U/L and P=.02; ALT: mean 113.09, SD 33.31 vs 156.35, SD 73.66 U/L and P=.004). The posttreatment platelet count was significantly higher in the NAC group (median 31.50, IQR 19.00-50.15 G/L vs 17.00, IQR 8.75-36.23 G/L; P=.001). The median increase in platelet count was also greater in the NAC group (15.05, IQR 7.05-26.10 G/L vs 6.95, IQR 4.22-15.43 G/L; P=.001). No severe infusion-related adverse events were documented during the study period. CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective, nonrandomized comparative study, intravenous NAC administration was associated with shorter hospitalization and lower posttreatment aminotransferase levels in adult patients with dengue fever and marked aminotransferase elevation. However, the nonrandomized design and potential for confounding limit causal inference. Larger, multicenter randomized controlled trials are warranted to clarify the therapeutic role of NAC in dengue-related hepatic complications.

papers.title_zh: 转氨酶显着升高的 登革热 患者静脉注射 N-乙酰半胱氨酸:前瞻性比较研究
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Dengue fever can lead to significant hepatic involvement and marked aminotransferase elevation and is associated with increased morbidity and prolonged hospitalization. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) has been proposed as a supportive therapy for dengue-induced liver injury. However, prospective comparative evidence from endemic regions such as Vietnam remains limited. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the association between intravenous NAC administration and clinical outcomes (primarily length of hospital stay), as well as the secondary effects of NAC on liver transaminase levels (posttreatment aspartate aminotransferase [AST] and alanine aminotransferase [ALT] and their changes from baseline) and platelet recovery in patients with dengue fever with marked aminotransferase elevation (AST or ALT ≥400 U/L). METHODS: A prospective, nonrandomized comparative study was conducted at the Department of Tropical Diseases, Viet Tiep Hospital, Hai Phong, Vietnam, from June to December 2024. A total of 128 adult patients with laboratory-confirmed dengue fever and marked aminotransferase elevation (AST and/or ALT ≥400 U/L) were enrolled. Treatment allocation was not randomized and was determined by the treating physicians based on aminotransferase elevation and overall clinical condition. Patients received either intravenous NAC (100 mg per kilogram per day) plus standard supportive care (NAC group; n=68) or standard care alone (non-NAC group; n=60). The primary outcome was length of hospital stay. Secondary outcomes included liver transaminase levels and platelet recovery at discharge. RESULTS: Baseline AST, ALT, bilirubin, and international normalized ratio values were broadly comparable between groups, although several clinical and hematological characteristics differed at baseline. The NAC group had a significantly shorter hospital stay (mean 5.01, SD 1.28 vs 6.12, SD 1.25 days; P<.001). The AST and ALT levels were significantly lower in the NAC group (AST: mean 154.83, SD 67.22 vs 184.62, SD 79.88 U/L and P=.02; ALT: mean 113.09, SD 33.31 vs 156.35, SD 73.66 U/L and P=.004). The posttreatment platelet count was significantly higher in the NAC group (median 31.50, IQR 19.00-50.15 G/L vs 17.00, IQR 8.75-36.23 G/L; P=.001). The median increase in platelet count was also greater in the NAC group (15.05, IQR 7.05-26.10 G/L vs 6.95, IQR 4.22-15.43 G/L; P=.001). No severe infusion-related adverse events were documented during the study period. CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective, nonrandomized comparative study, intravenous NAC administration was associated with shorter hospitalization and lower posttreatment aminotransferase levels in adult patients with dengue fever and marked aminotransferase elevation. However, the nonrandomized design and potential for confounding limit causal inference. Larger, multicenter randomized controlled trials are warranted to clarify the therapeutic role of NAC in dengue-related hepatic complications.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:登革热可导致显著的肝脏受累和明显的转氨酶升高,并与发病率增加和住院时间延长有关。N-乙酰半胱氨酸(NAC)已被提出作为登革热诱导的肝损伤的支持性治疗。然而,在越南等流行地区仍缺乏前瞻性比较证据。目的:本研究旨在评估静脉注射NAC与临床结局(主要为住院时间)之间的关联,以及NAC对肝转氨酶水平(治疗后天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶[AST]和丙氨酸氨基转移酶[ALT]及其与基线值的变化)和血小板恢复的二次影响。方法:本研究于2024年6月至12月在越南海防市 Viet Tiep 医院热带病科进行,是一项前瞻性、非随机的比较研究。共纳入128名实验室确诊的登革热成人患者,且具有显著的转氨酶升高(AST和/或ALT≥400 U/L)。治疗的分配未进行随机化,而是由治疗医生根据转氨酶升高程度和总体临床状况决定。患者接受静脉注射NAC(每日100 mg/千克)加标准支持治疗(NAC组,n=68)或仅接受标准治疗(非NAC组,n=60)。主要结局是住院时间。次要结局包括出院时的肝转氨酶水平和血小板恢复情况。结果:基线AST、ALT、胆红素和国际标准化比值在两组间大致可比,尽管一些临床和血液学特征在基线时存在差异。NAC组的住院时间明显较短(均值5.01天,标准差1.28 vs 6.12天,标准差1.25;P<.001)。NAC组的AST和ALT水平显著降低(AST:均值154.83 U/L,标准差67.22 vs 184.62 U/L,标准差79.88,P=.02;ALT:均值113.09 U/L,标准差33.31 vs 156.35 U/L,标准差73.66,P=.004)。治疗后血小板计数在NAC组显著更高(中位数31.50 G/L,四分位距19.00-50.15 vs 17.00 G/L,四分位距8.75-36.23,P=.001)。NAC组的血小板计数中位数增加量也更大(15.05 G/L,四分位距7.05-26.10 vs 6.95 G/L,四分位距4.22-15.43,P=.001)。研究期间未记录严重的输注相关不良事件。结论:在这项前瞻性、非随机的比较研究中,静脉注射NAC与登革热成人患者显著转氨酶升高后的住院时间缩短和治疗后转氨酶水平降低有关。然而,非随机设计和潜在的混杂因素限制了因果推论。需要更大规模、多中心的随机对照试验来明确NAC在登革热相关肝损伤治疗中的作用。

papers.title: Tracking two decades of global dengue virus lineage dynamics
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) is genetically diverse, consisting of four antigenically distinct serotypes and extensive sub-serotype variation that can influence epidemiology and control. As DENV continues to expand globally, there is an urgent need to characterize the dynamics of distinct DENV genetic lineages, including their persistence, establishment, and spread. Using a standardized DENV lineage nomenclature system and 37,828 publicly available DENV genomes sampled from 2000-2024, we classified sequences across nine global regions to construct a comprehensive resource of regional lineage distributions over time. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to track the dynamics of dengue virus (DENV) genetic lineages over two decades, addressing the need to characterize the persistence, establishment, and spread of distinct DENV genetic lineages globally.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a standardized DENV lineage nomenclature system and analyzed 37,828 publicly available DENV genomes sampled from 2000 to 2024 across nine global regions.
analysis.methods: Sequences were classified across nine global regions to construct a comprehensive resource of regional lineage distributions over time, using a standardized DENV lineage nomenclature system.
analysis.main_results: The study found marked regional differences in lineage diversity, with higher lineage richness in Southeast and East Asia than in the Americas. It also showed that COVID-19-related disruptions were associated with decreased regional lineage persistence and detection of new lineages during 2020-2021, followed by rebounds after 2022 and substantial lineage turnover in some regions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating how standardized lineage classification enables global tracking of emerging DENV diversity and supports targeted genomic surveillance, identifying a small set of globally expansive lineages.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform targeted genomic surveillance and support the development of strategies to monitor and control DENV diversity and spread.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the reliance on publicly available sequences, which may not be representative of all DENV lineages, and the potential for biases in sampling. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study tracked the dynamics of dengue virus genetic lineages over two decades, finding regional differences in lineage diversity and impacts of COVID-19 disruptions. Standardized lineage classification supports global surveillance and control strategies.

papers.title_zh: 追踪全球 登革病毒 谱系动态二十年
papers.source_body_en: Dengue virus (DENV) is genetically diverse, consisting of four antigenically distinct serotypes and extensive sub-serotype variation that can influence epidemiology and control. As DENV continues to expand globally, there is an urgent need to characterize the dynamics of distinct DENV genetic lineages, including their persistence, establishment, and spread. Using a standardized DENV lineage nomenclature system and 37,828 publicly available DENV genomes sampled from 2000-2024, we classified sequences across nine global regions to construct a comprehensive resource of regional lineage distributions over time. We found marked regional differences in lineage diversity, with higher lineage richness in Southeast and East Asia than in the Americas. We further showed that COVID-19-related disruptions were associated with decreased regional lineage persistence and detection of new lineages during 2020-2021, followed by rebounds after 2022 and, in some regions, substantial lineage turnover. Finally, we identified a small set of globally expansive (cosmopolitan) lineages that are over-represented in available sequences, including five first-order minor lineages detected in at least seven of nine regions: 3III_B.3, 2II_F.1, 2II_A.1, 1III_A.3, and 1I_K.3. Together, these results demonstrate how standardized lineage classification enables global tracking of emerging DENV diversity and supports targeted genomic surveillance.

papers.title: Vector competence for dengue-2 virus of permethrin resistant/ susceptible Aedes aegypti sub-populations from selected sites in Lamu County, Kenya
papers.abstract: Dengue virus, primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, is endemic in Lamu County. There is currently no definitive treatment for dengue; therefore, vector control remains the most effective method to curb transmission. Prolonged exposure of Ae. aegypti to insecticides may confer resistance. This study aimed to determine the levels of resistance to permethrin, a commonly used insecticide, and to compare the vectorial competence and genetic differences of resistant versus susceptible populations for dengue-2 virus. aegypti mosquitoes were collected from Lamu (Shela, Hindi, and Mokowe) using traps and assayed for permethrin resistance/ susceptibility. WHO insecticide resistance assays were conducted. The mosquitoes (F 2 ) were exposed to dengue-2 infectious bloodmeals and fully engorged mosquitoes selected, incubated for up to 21 days, and tested for infection and dissemination by plaque assay. Individual legs were dissected from 31 female (F 0 ) mosquitoes for isolation of genomic DNA. Polymerase Chain Reaction was used to amplify the target mitochondrial DNA using HCO2198 and LCO1490 primers. The amplicons were Sanger sequenced to determine genetic diversity. The Shela sub-population displayed susceptibility (>98% mortality), whereas the Hindi and Mokowe sub-populations exhibited resistance, with mortality rates of 47% and 37.6%, respectively. Of the mosquitoes from Hindi (n = 60); Mokowe (n = 90); and Shela (n = 130), n = 14 (23%), n = 24 (27%), and n = 40 (31%) respectively, had midgut infections with dengue-2; while n = 12 (20%), n = 11 (12%), and n = 21 (16%) respectively had disseminated infection. Genetic analysis showed that all the samples were Ae. aegypti formosus sub-species. Haplotype diversity was high at 1.0 while nucleotide diversity was low at 0.01184. These findings suggest Ae. aegypti formosus sub-species is prevalent in Lamu County. The study also demonstrated high infection and dissemination rates among the Ae. aegypti sub- populations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the vector competence of permethrin-resistant and -susceptible Aedes aegypti sub-populations in Lamu County, Kenya, for dengue-2 virus. The research highlights the importance of vector control in dengue prevention, as there is no definitive treatment. Mosquitoes were collected from three sites and tested for resistance using WHO assays. The study found that Shela mosquitoes were highly susceptible, while Hindi and Mokowe populations showed resistance. papers.title_zh: 媒介 肯尼亚拉穆县选定地点的氯菊酯抗性/易感埃及伊蚊亚群对登革热 2 病毒的能力
papers.source_body_en: Dengue virus, primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, is endemic in Lamu County. There is currently no definitive treatment for dengue; therefore, vector control remains the most effective method to curb transmission. Prolonged exposure of Ae. aegypti to insecticides may confer resistance. This study aimed to determine the levels of resistance to permethrin, a commonly used insecticide, and to compare the vectorial competence and genetic differences of resistant versus susceptible populations for dengue-2 virus. aegypti mosquitoes were collected from Lamu (Shela, Hindi, and Mokowe) using traps and assayed for permethrin resistance/ susceptibility. WHO insecticide resistance assays were conducted. The mosquitoes (F 2 ) were exposed to dengue-2 infectious bloodmeals and fully engorged mosquitoes selected, incubated for up to 21 days, and tested for infection and dissemination by plaque assay. Individual legs were dissected from 31 female (F 0 ) mosquitoes for isolation of genomic DNA. Polymerase Chain Reaction was used to amplify the target mitochondrial DNA using HCO2198 and LCO1490 primers. The amplicons were Sanger sequenced to determine genetic diversity. The Shela sub-population displayed susceptibility (>98% mortality), whereas the Hindi and Mokowe sub-populations exhibited resistance, with mortality rates of 47% and 37.6%, respectively. Of the mosquitoes from Hindi (n = 60); Mokowe (n = 90); and Shela (n = 130), n = 14 (23%), n = 24 (27%), and n = 40 (31%) respectively, had midgut infections with dengue-2; while n = 12 (20%), n = 11 (12%), and n = 21 (16%) respectively had disseminated infection. Genetic analysis showed that all the samples were Ae. aegypti formosus sub-species. Haplotype diversity was high at 1.0 while nucleotide diversity was low at 0.01184. These findings suggest Ae. aegypti formosus sub-species is prevalent in Lamu County. The study also demonstrated high infection and dissemination rates among the Ae. aegypti sub- populations.

papers.title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.
papers.abstract: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.

papers.abstract_zh: 蚊媒虫媒病毒(包括登革病毒(DENV)、寨卡病毒(ZIKV)和基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV))构成了日益增长的全球健康负担,但目前针对这些感染的特异性抗病毒药物疗法尚不普及。这种未满足的医疗需求凸显了从生物相关来源(如植物来源的天然产物)中识别新型抗病毒药物化合物的重要性。本研究采用基于生物活性的筛选方法,对八种茄科植物的甲醇提取物进行分析,以鉴定具有抗病毒药物活性的化合物,针对Vero细胞中DENV-2的感染。五种提取物显著降低了病毒的感染性,其中Solanum ovalifolium和Cestrum sp.在非细胞毒性浓度下实现了完全抑制。随后的分级和纯化过程分离出四种螺甾烷型甾体皂苷,其结构通过超高效液相色谱-二极管阵列检测-质谱(UPLC-DAD-MS)和一维/二维核磁共振(1D/2D NMR)光谱进行表征。功能实验表明,这些化合物抑制DENV复制,表现为病毒RNA水平、NS1和NS3蛋白表达以及传染性病毒滴度的显著下降。阶段特异性分析显示,其抗病毒药物活性主要与病毒生命周期的细胞内阶段相关,这与抑制病毒复制和/或蛋白质加工一致。分子对接分析支持这些发现,预测这些化合物与关键病毒酶(特别是NS5 RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶和NS3解旋酶/蛋白酶)具有有利的相互作用。重要的是,分离出的化合物对ZIKV和CHIKV也表现出抗病毒药物活性,表明其具有跨虫媒病毒的疗效。综上所述,这些发现表明螺甾烷皂苷是具有前景的抗病毒药物骨架,并支持其进一步开发为广谱抗病毒药物药物。

papers.title: Real-world safety of dengue vaccines in Brazil: A pharmacovigilance study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The expansion of dengue vaccination strategies in Brazil, including the introduction of the Butantan dengue vaccine (DV), has reinforced the importance of post-marketing safety surveillance. We aimed to characterize reporting patterns of adverse events following immunization (AEFIs) and immunization errors associated with dengue vaccines in Brazil. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective observational study using records of AEFIs associated with dengue vaccines reported to the Brazilian Ministry of Health through June 2026. AEFIs were classified as serious or non-serious according to national surveillance criteria, and immunization errors were analyzed separately. RESULTS: Among 47,666 individuals with reported AEFIs or immunization errors following dengue vaccination, 525 (1.1%) experienced at least one serious AEFI, 43,043 (90.3%) reported non-serious AEFIs, and 4098 (8.6%) were classified as immunization errors. Serious AEFIs were uncommon across vaccine platforms. Among recipients of Butantan-DV, the most frequent serious AEFIs were skin manifestations, central nervous system symptoms, and myalgia or arthralgia. Among recipients of other dengue vaccines, skin manifestations, anaphylaxis or bronchospasm, and respiratory symptoms predominated. Non-serious AEFIs were mainly exanthema, headache, and pruritus. Immunization errors were primarily related to inappropriate age at vaccination, shortened intervals between doses, and incorrect routes of administration. Reporting rates increased during the expansion of dengue vaccination activities in 2026. CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide pharmacovigilance study, dengue vaccines demonstrated a favorable safety profile, with serious adverse events accounting for only a small proportion of reported events. These findings support the implementation of dengue vaccination programs while reinforcing the importance of ongoing surveillance to identify rare safety signals and reduce preventable immunization errors.

We aimed to characterize reporting patterns of adverse events following immunization (AEFIs) and immunization errors associated with dengue vaccines in Brazil. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective observational study using records of AEFIs associated with dengue vaccines reported to the Brazilian Ministry of Health through June 2026. AEFIs were classified as serious or non-serious according to national surveillance criteria, and immunization errors were analyzed separately. RESULTS: Among 47,666 individuals with reported AEFIs or immunization errors following dengue vaccination, 525 (1.1%) experienced at least one serious AEFI, 43,043 (90.3%) reported non-serious AEFIs, and 4098 (8.6%) were classified as immunization errors. Serious AEFIs were uncommon across vaccine platforms. Among recipients of Butantan-DV, the most frequent serious AEFIs were skin manifestations, central nervous system symptoms, and myalgia or arthralgia. Among recipients of other dengue vaccines, skin manifestations, anaphylaxis or bronchospasm, and respiratory symptoms predominated. Non-serious AEFIs were mainly exanthema, headache, and pruritus. Immunization errors were primarily related to inappropriate age at vaccination, shortened intervals between doses, and incorrect routes of administration. Reporting rates increased during the expansion of dengue vaccination activities in 2026. CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide pharmacovigilance study, dengue vaccines demonstrated a favorable safety profile, with serious adverse events accounting for only a small proportion of reported events. These findings support the implementation of dengue vaccination programs while reinforcing the importance of ongoing surveillance to identify rare safety signals and reduce preventable immunization errors.

papers.title: A Cross-Sectional Study in Northeast India to Assess Malaria, Scrub Typhus, and Dengue in Patients with Acute Febrile Illness Using ELISA
papers.abstract: Abstract Aim Acute febrile illness (AFI) is a major reason for hospitalization in tropical and subtropical regions. Overlapping clinical features might also lead to confusion about the diagnosis of AFI. In India, dengue, scrub typhus, and malaria continue to be the most prevalent causes. Early laboratory validation using ELISA-based assays is essential for timely medication and a reduction in morbidity and death. Methods Using commercial ELISA kits to detect dengue NS1 antigen, dengue IgM antibodies, scrub typhus IgM antibodies, and malaria pLDH antigen in accordance with manufacturer instructions, a cross-sectional study of 200 patients presenting with AFI—95 urban and 105 rural residents—was carried out. Data on demographics, residential status, and length of fever were recorded, and statistical analysis was carried out using PAST software. Result The results showed that 51% of the patients were male and 49% were female. Patients from rural areas made up a higher proportion (53%) than those from metropolitan areas (47%). 16% of patients in cities were positive for dengue NS1, 7% for dengue IgM, 12% for scrub typhus, and 17% for malaria. Dengue (18%), scrub typhus (19%), and malaria (22%) were more prevalent among rural people. Longer fevers, particularly those lasting between 6 and 14 days, were related to greater positives. Malaria and scrub typhus were the leading causes of AFI. Conclusion ELISA-based diagnostics are useful for early detection of AFI etiology. Higher rural incidence highlights the importance of improved monitoring, early diagnostic access, and focused public health interventions.

papers.title: A TLR2-associated entry pathway promotes productive dengue virus serotype 2 infection and inflammatory responses in classical monocytes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Severe dengue is characterized by systemic inflammation and vascular leakage. Recent evidence indicates that Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) supports early steps of dengue virus (DENV) infection in monocytes, whereas intracellular viral RNA sensing drives much of the subsequent inflammatory response. However, whether this entry-associated function of TLR2 differs among human monocyte subsets remains unknown. Here, we investigated how the TLR2 axis regulates DENV serotype 2 (DENV2) infection and inflammatory output in purified primary human monocytes and sorted monocyte subsets. Blocking TLR2 at the cell surface or targeting its intracellular TIR domain reduced virus-cell association, productive infection, and the release of inflammatory and antiviral mediators. Among TLR2-associated receptors, CD14 and, to a lesser extent, CD36 contributed to efficient infection, whereas TLR1, TLR6, and TLR10 were dispensable under the conditions tested. Notably, TLR2 blockade reduced viral production and cytokine release in CD16 − classical monocytes but not in pooled CD16 + monocytes, identifying a subset-specific dependence on the TLR2 axis. TLR3 contributed to inflammatory and antiviral responses without affecting viral replication, consistent with post-entry recognition of viral RNA. Finally, blocking the TLR2 axis during monocyte infection prevented the loss of endothelial barrier integrity induced by monocyte-derived soluble mediators. Together, these findings identify a TLR2-associated entry route that preferentially supports productive DENV2 infection in classical monocytes and thereby enables RNA-sensor-dependent inflammatory responses that compromise endothelial function. AUTHOR SUMMARY Monocytes are major targets of dengue virus infection and can release inflammatory mediators that weaken the endothelial barrier, a hallmark of severe dengue. We recently showed that TLR2 acts early during direct and antibody-enhanced dengue virus infection, whereas intracellular receptors that detect viral RNA contribute to the subsequent inflammatory response. Here, we show that this pathway is not used equally by all monocytes. Classical CD16 − monocytes depended strongly on the TLR2 axis for productive infection and cytokine release, whereas pooled CD16 + monocytes did not. CD14 and, more modestly, CD36 contributed to infection in purified monocytes. Blocking TLR2 during infection also prevented monocyte-derived factors from disrupting endothelial barrier function. papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 重症登革热 的特点是全身炎症和血管渗漏。最近的证据表明,Toll 样受体 2 (TLR2) 支持单核细胞 登革病毒 (DENV) 感染的早期步骤,而细胞内病毒 RNA 传感则驱动大部分后续炎症反应。然而,TLR2 的这种进入相关功能在人类单核细胞亚群中是否存在差异仍然未知。在这里,我们研究了 TLR2 轴如何调节纯化的原代人单核细胞和分选的单核细胞亚群中的 DENV 血清型 2 (DENV2) 感染和炎症输出。阻断细胞表面的 TLR2 或靶向其细胞内 TIR 结构域可减少病毒与细胞的关联、有效感染以及炎症和 抗病毒药物 介质的释放。在 TLR2 相关受体中,CD14 以及较小程度上的 CD36 有助于有效感染,而 TLR1、TLR6 和 TLR10 在测试条件下是可有可无的。值得注意的是,TLR2 阻断减少了 CD16 - 经典单核细胞中的病毒产生和细胞因子释放,但在混合的 CD16 + 单核细胞中却没有,从而确定了对 TLR2 轴的子集特异性依赖性。TLR3 在不影响病毒复制的情况下促进炎症和 抗病毒药物 反应,这与病毒 RNA 的进入后识别一致。最后,在单核细胞感染过程中阻断 TLR2 轴可以防止单核细胞衍生的可溶性介质诱导的内皮屏障完整性丧失。总之,这些发现确定了一种与 TLR2 相关的进入途径,该途径优先支持经典单核细胞中的高效 DENV2 感染,从而实现 RNA 传感器依赖性炎症反应,从而损害内皮功能。作者摘要 单核细胞是 重症登革热 感染的主要目标,可以释放削弱内皮屏障的炎症介质,这是 重症登革热 的标志。我们最近表明,TLR2 在直接感染和抗体增强的 登革病毒 感染过程中早期发挥作用,而检测病毒 RNA 的细胞内受体则有助于随后的炎症反应。在这里,我们表明并非所有单核细胞都平等地使用该途径。经典的 CD16 - 单核细胞强烈依赖于 TLR2 轴来进行有效感染和细胞因子释放,而合并的 CD16 + 单核细胞则不然。CD14 和更温和的 CD36 有助于纯化单核细胞的感染。在感染过程中阻断 TLR2 还可以防止单核细胞衍生因子破坏内皮屏障功能。这些发现表明,单核细胞特性决定了 登革病毒 如何进入细胞以及感染与潜在有害炎症的耦合程度。

papers.title: Computational Insights Into the Conformational Dynamics of the Dengue Virus Capsid Protein.
papers.abstract: The Dengue virus (DENV) capsid protein plays an important role in the viral lifecycle, including encapsidation of the genome, recruitment of lipid droplets, and assembly of particles. Capsid protein includes a hydrophobic pocket, which plays a central role in these functions and switches between closed and open conformations. This work studies the conformational change pathway of the capsid protein, specifically how the molecular mechanisms controlling the opening and closing of the hydrophobic pocket are controlled. By using a combination of different types of molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling methods, we share insights on the structural rearrangements that play a crucial role in governing these transitions. Our results show that lipid binding modulates the accessibility of the hydrophobic pocket through environmental cues. In the open conformation, the pocket is involved in the interaction with lipids, stabilization of capsid dimers, and the promotion of immature virus assembly. Conversely, the closed conformation protects the hydrophobic pocket from the surrounding aqueous media as also preventing premature interactions in the solution phase that might disrupt protein stability. Such insights allow a deep understanding of capsid protein's conformational dynamics and represent a promising set of potent targets for antiviral strategies aiming to interfere with its functional transitions.

papers.abstract_original: The Dengue virus (DENV) capsid protein plays an important role in the viral lifecycle, including encapsidation of the genome, recruitment of lipid droplets, and assembly of particles. Capsid protein includes a hydrophobic pocket, which plays a central role in these functions and switches between closed and open conformations. This work studies the conformational change pathway of the capsid protein, specifically how the molecular mechanisms controlling the opening and closing of the hydrophobic pocket are controlled. By using a combination of different types of molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling methods, we share insights on the structural rearrangements that play a crucial role in governing these transitions. Our results show that lipid binding modulates the accessibility of the hydrophobic pocket through environmental cues. In the open conformation, the pocket is involved in the interaction with lipids, stabilization of capsid dimers, and the promotion of immature virus assembly. Conversely, the closed conformation protects the hydrophobic pocket from the surrounding aqueous media as also preventing premature interactions in the solution phase that might disrupt protein stability. Such insights allow a deep understanding of capsid protein's conformational dynamics and represent a promising set of potent targets for antiviral strategies aiming to interfere with its functional transitions.

Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. New tools can help detect risk earlier and prevent disease, but their usefulness depends on local capacity, safety monitoring, affordability, environmental considerations, and sustained implementation. papers.full_text: Abstract Since 2020, viruses spread by mosquitoes and biting midges have become a larger and less predictable public health challenge. Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. New tools can help detect risk earlier and prevent disease, but their usefulness depends on local capacity, safety monitoring, affordability, environmental considerations, and sustained implementation. The next phase of arbovirus control will depend on using these tools strategically, equitably, and before outbreaks overwhelm health systems. Introduction Arthropod-borne viruses, particularly dengue, chikungunya, Zika, yellow fever, and West Nile, remained major infectious threats during the COVID-19 era. Since 2020, record dengue seasons in the Americas, resurgent chikungunya, and continued outbreaks of West Nile and yellow fever underscored the importance of viruses transmitted by Culex and Aedes mosquitoes in tropical and subtropical regions. The re-emergence of Oropouche virus in non-endemic areas and continued concern about Mayaro virus further broadened the arboviral landscape beyond dengue, chikungunya, and Zika, which dominated attention a decade ago1. Recent multi-pathogen risk maps estimate that roughly 5.7 billion people live in areas environmentally suitable for dengue, chikungunya, and Zika virus transmission, and about 1.5 billion in areas suitable for urban yellow fever virus transmission, overlapping with dense urbanization, informal settlements, and major travel corridors2. For clinicians and public health practitioners, it is no longer helpful to think in terms of a single “dengue belt”. Most large cities in the tropics, and an increasing number in temperate zones, now face a shifting mix of arboviral threats. Since our 2020 overview of arboviruses and their vectors1, five broad changes have emerged that are especially relevant to clinicians and public health programs. First, dengue still accounts for much of the global burden, but the resurgence of chikungunya and the re-emergence of Oropouche and other viruses show how quickly the arboviral landscape can shift. Second, surveillance and diagnostics are becoming more anticipatory, with environmental, digital, and laboratory-based tools complementing routine clinical and public health reporting. Third, vaccination policy for dengue, yellow fever, and chikungunya is increasingly shaped by implementation and safety monitoring, while therapeutics remain limited. Fourth, competent vectors are being documented across a broader geographic range and are showing greater behavioral and ecological flexibility. Fifth, Aedes-focused vector control now has stronger evidence for reducing dengue risk, with Wolbachia replacement providing the clearest large-scale disease-endpoint evidence and several other approaches showing promising but more heterogeneous evidence. These five changes and their practical implications are summarized in Table 1. Figure 1 provides a complementary visual synthesis, positioning key developments along a continuum from public health challenges to opportunities, with mixed or evolving areas between them. Methods We conducted a narrative review of literature and public health guidance on arboviruses and their vectors published from January 1, 2020, through June 30, 2026. The review aimed to identify major developments since a prior 2020 overview, emphasizing findings relevant to clinicians, surveillance programs, vaccine and vector-control policy, and public health practice. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar using combinations of terms related to arboviruses, pathogens, vectors, surveillance, diagnostics, vaccines, therapeutics, and vector control. Search terms included combinations of “arbovirus”, “arthropod-borne virus”, “dengue”, “chikungunya”, “Zika”, “yellow fever”, “West Nile”, “Oropouche”, “Mayaro”, “Japanese encephalitis”, “Powassan”, “La Crosse”, “Aedes aegypti”, “Aedes albopictus”, “Culex”, “Culicoides”, “vector competence”, “range expansion”, “genomic surveillance”, “wastewater”, “environmental DNA”, “diagnostics”, “multiplex PCR”, “vaccine”, “therapeutic”, “Wolbachia”, “sterile insect technique”, “spatial repellent”, “pyriproxyfen”, and “indoor residual spraying”. Searches were supplemented by reference-list review and targeted review of surveillance, guidance, and regulatory documents from the World Health Organization, Pan American Health Organization, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and European Medicines Agency. We prioritized primary studies, clinical trials, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, major surveillance reports, policy recommendations, and regulatory documents that described substantial changes since 2020 or had direct implications for clinical care, surveillance, vaccination, therapeutics, vector ecology, or vector control. We excluded articles outside the 2020–2026 period unless needed for historical context, articles not directly relevant to human arboviral disease or vector-borne public health practice, studies focused only on basic virology or animal models without clear clinical or public health relevance, and duplicate or superseded guidance documents. Preprints were identified through Google Scholar, reference-list review, and coauthor expertise rather than a separate systematic search of preprint servers. They were considered only when they addressed rapidly evolving developments not yet represented in peer-reviewed literature and were identified as preprints in the reference list. One author (Z.J.M.) conducted the initial searches and screening. All coauthors reviewed selected evidence within their areas of expertise and suggested additional sources. Final inclusion was based on relevance to the five themes highlighted in this review and consensus among the authors. Because this was a narrative review rather than a systematic review or meta-analysis, we did not perform duplicate screening, formal risk-of-bias assessment, exhaustive evidence mapping, or pooled quantitative synthesis. Change 1: Dengue still dominates, but the resurgence and expansion of other arboviruses remain a threat Dengue remains the most widespread arboviral disease. In 2024, more than 14.4 million dengue cases, including over 52,000 severe cases and about 11,000 deaths, were reported globally—the highest annual totals in modern records and a major strain on health systems3. Dengue virus (DENV) serotype circulation has also shifted, with re-emergence of DENV-3 and increased detection of DENV-4 in parts of the Americas4,5. Genomic analyses suggest that many recent epidemics have been driven by overlapping lineages rather than by a single variant6,7. Intense dengue seasons therefore rarely have a single explanation. They can reflect the combined effects of co-circulating serotypes and lineages, changing population immunity, and ecological conditions that favor vector abundance. Immunologic studies have further clarified why some DENV infections progress to severe disease. Prior DENV infection is known to influence the risk of severe disease after subsequent infection. Newer work suggests that prior Zika virus (ZIKV) infection and qualitative features of the antibody response, including IgG afucosylation, may also shape risk8,9,10. Nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) also contributes to vascular leak and remains an important diagnostic target, reinforcing guidance to use NS1- or RNA-based tests early in illness when available11. Chikungunya has re-emerged as a major clinical and public health problem. Since 2020, large outbreaks have caused hundreds of thousands of cases in Brazil, Paraguay, Bolivia, the Indian Ocean region, and parts of South and Southeast Asia12. Many patients experience disabling arthralgia and fatigue after acute infection, sometimes lasting months to years13. Long-term morbidity is therefore a substantial part of chikungunya’s burden, even when mortality is low. Viral changes that enhance replication in Ae. albopictus are thought to have contributed to transmission in temperate regions14,15,16, while recent longitudinal cohorts and mechanistic studies have better characterized the frequency, persistence, inflammatory phenotypes, and biology of chronic chikungunya sequelae17,18. Since 2020, Zika and yellow fever viruses have caused fewer large outbreaks than dengue or chikungunya but remain clinically important. ZIKV continues to circulate at low levels, with sporadic detections in Africa, Asia, and the Americas19,20. Long-term follow-up has documented sustained neurologic and developmental challenges in children with congenital Zika syndrome, and newer studies suggest that even some children with in utero exposure without classic congenital Zika syndrome may remain at risk for developmental delay21,22. Yellow fever outbreaks in Africa and the Americas have likewise highlighted vulnerabilities where vaccination coverage has lagged, routine services have been disrupted, or vaccine supply has been constrained23,24. A single dose of yellow fever vaccine remains highly protective. Oropouche, Mayaro, and other watch-list viruses have become more prominent. In 2024–2025, Oropouche virus caused large outbreaks in the Americas beyond its historic Amazon range, including in urban areas, with substantial spatial heterogeneity in risk shaped by demographic, climatic, and environmental conditions25. Most cases are mild, but complications can include vertical transmission, possible adverse pregnancy outcomes, neurological manifestations, and rarely, death26,27. In urban and peri-urban settings, transmission is driven mainly by the biting midge Culicoides paraensis28. Mayaro virus still circulates mainly in forest and rural transmission cycles29, but laboratory evidence of efficient transmission by Ae. aegypti and Ae. albopictus raises concern about urban spillover potential30,31. Because early presentations overlap with dengue and other nonspecific acute febrile illnesses, these infections are likely to be misclassified without molecular or reliable serologic diagnostics. Arboviral diversity is also evident beyond the tropics: in the United States, Powassan virus disease remains rare but has increased in recent years, while La Crosse virus continues to cause recurrent seasonal neuroinvasive disease, particularly among children32,33. Clinicians should use the patient’s clinical presentation and epidemiologic risk factors such as travel history to guide testing considerations for dengue as well as less commonly diagnosed arboviral infections. Consultation with public health authorities may also be beneficial when rare arboviral infections are suspected to help determine the most appropriate diagnostic testing. For example, suspect case definition criteria have recently been developed for Oropouche virus and include compatible illness with travel to an area with transmission within two weeks of initial symptom onset, recognizing that patients may experience recurrent nonspecific febrile illness or, less frequently, recurrent neurologic symptoms28,34,35. Current understanding of arboviral risk reflects both transmission and the capacity to detect it36. Because many infections are asymptomatic or clinically nonspecific, observed patterns depend on which clinical presentations prompt testing, which diagnostic assays and case definitions are used, how broadly vector and genomic surveillance is conducted, and how completely cases are reported. Broader, integrated surveillance can reveal epidemiologic shifts, genetic turnover, unusual transmission events, and geographic spread that remain undetected where capacity is limited, even when competent vectors are present. Recent events show what this means in practice. In the United States, genomic investigation identified the first known human infection involving West Nile virus lineage 3, detected together with lineage 1b in a patient with neuroinvasive disease37. In northern Italy, genomic surveillance identified a newly introduced West Nile virus lineage 1 strain in 2021 and documented its rapid spread in a region already co-endemic for lineage 238. The 2022 Japanese encephalitis outbreak on the Australian mainland, which included the first locally acquired mainland cases detected since 1998, was recognized through coordinated human, animal, and vector surveillance and indicated geographic expansion rather than previously unrecognized longstanding transmission39. Taken together, these trends argue against a narrow focus on familiar arboviruses or interpretation of raw case counts in isolation. For clinicians and public health programs, the practical challenge is no longer only rising dengue burden, but recognizing a wider and shifting set of clinically similar infections—many of which may be misclassified or missed where surveillance and diagnostic capacity are uneven—and interpreting trends using clinical, laboratory, genomic, entomological, and severity data together. Change 2: Surveillance and diagnostics are becoming more anticipatory A second major change since 2020 is the movement toward surveillance and diagnostic tools that can identify vector presence, transmission risk, or outbreaks earlier than routine case reporting alone. Traditional case and vector surveillance remain the backbone of arboviral control. Some newer tools are approaching operational decision support, while others remain research-based, in pilot use, or limited to specialized settings. Their value depends on field validation, affordability, local calibration, and integration into routine surveillance and response systems. Integrated risk maps and outbreak forecasting systems are among the tools closest to operational use. Although related, they answer different operational questions. Risk maps primarily identify where transmission risk or vulnerability is concentrated, using combinations of epidemiologic, entomologic, demographic, environmental, mobility, and other surveillance data to guide geographically targeted surveillance, vaccination, and resource allocation2,40. Forecasting systems add an explicit future time horizon. D-MOSS in Vietnam combines recent dengue case counts with seasonal climate forecasts, Earth-observation data, and sociodemographic predictors to generate monthly province-level forecasts of dengue incidence and outbreak-threshold exceedance one to six months ahead41. Its prospective evaluation illustrates the movement from retrospective modeling toward operational decision support, although performance varies by setting, season, lead time, and threshold choice. Routine surveillance of dengue diagnosed in travelers after their return to the United States provides a different but complementary signal. It uses likely countries of exposure to identify sustained increases in destination-specific risk and can complement local reporting where official data are delayed or incomplete42. Other approaches remain earlier in the research-to-implementation pathway. Environmental DNA methods are being explored for detecting Aedes, Culex, and other vector species in aquatic habitats, but their public health value remains uncertain because sampling, laboratory capacity, training requirements, action thresholds, and links to adult mosquito abundance or transmission risk remain incompletely defined43,44,45. Computer-vision and machine-learning approaches are also being tested for entomological surveillance. AI-enabled smart traps may support faster mosquito detection and classification, while satellite, street-view, and drone imagery may help identify likely breeding sites, such as rooftop tanks, tires, and gutters46,47,48,49,50. However, performance varies by species, setting, image quality, training data, maintenance requirements, and local infrastructure, and few systems have been evaluated against traditional surveillance methodologies for sustained routine use or impact on outbreak response. These tools are best viewed as complements to routine surveillance rather than replacements for it. Wastewater surveillance, scaled rapidly for SARS-CoV-2, is now being applied to arboviruses, but its role in public health practice remains uncertain. Several arboviruses, including dengue, chikungunya, and Zika, have been detected in wastewater, yet interpretation of these data is limited by poorly defined shedding dynamics, viral RNA degradation, and uncertain relationships between wastewater signals and incident human infection51,52,53,54. Current methods also cannot distinguish travel-associated from locally acquired infections, and sewer catchments may exceed the geographic scale at which vector-control interventions are implemented51. For arboviruses with non-human amplifying hosts, such as West Nile and Japanese encephalitis viruses, wastewater detections may reflect animal rather than human infections, further complicating interpretation55. Studies are needed to determine when wastewater signals are actionable, but possible use cases include early detection of novel pathogens introduced into new areas, which could trigger enhanced clinical and vector surveillance, and targeted agricultural applications, such as monitoring epizootic signals of Japanese encephalitis in pig-farm effluent56. Diagnostics have also advanced, but access remains uneven. High-sensitivity rapid tests, multiplex PCR platforms, next-generation sequencing, and multiplex serologic approaches are increasingly available in referral, research, and tertiary-care settings, while lower-cost locally produced assays and point-of-care multiplex platforms remain under development or early implementation in many settings57,58,59. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Since 2020, viruses spread by mosquitoes and biting midges have become a larger and less predictable public health challenge. Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. New tools can help detect risk earlier and prevent disease, but their usefulness depends on local capacity, safety monitoring, affordability, environmental considerations, and sustained implementation. The next phase of arbovirus control will depend on using these tools strategically, equitably, and before outbreaks overwhelm health systems. Introduction Arthropod-borne viruses, particularly dengue, chikungunya, Zika, yellow fever, and West Nile, remained major infectious threats during the COVID-19 era. Since 2020, record dengue seasons in the Americas, resurgent chikungunya, and continued outbreaks of West Nile and yellow fever underscored the importance of viruses transmitted by Culex and Aedes mosquitoes in tropical and subtropical regions. The re-emergence of Oropouche virus in non-endemic areas and continued concern about Mayaro virus further broadened the arboviral landscape beyond dengue, chikungunya, and Zika, which dominated attention a decade ago1. Recent multi-pathogen risk maps estimate that roughly 5.7 billion people live in areas environmentally suitable for dengue, chikungunya, and Zika virus transmission, and about 1.5 billion in areas suitable for urban yellow fever virus transmission, overlapping with dense urbanization, informal settlements, and major travel corridors2. For clinicians and public health practitioners, it is no longer helpful to think in terms of a single “dengue belt”. Most large cities in the tropics, and an increasing number in temperate zones, now face a shifting mix of arboviral threats. Since our 2020 overview of arboviruses and their vectors1, five broad changes have emerged that are especially relevant to clinicians and public health programs. First, dengue still accounts for much of the global burden, but the resurgence of chikungunya and the re-emergence of Oropouche and other viruses show how quickly the arboviral landscape can shift. Second, surveillance and diagnostics are becoming more anticipatory, with environmental, digital, and laboratory-based tools complementing routine clinical and public health reporting. Third, vaccination policy for dengue, yellow fever, and chikungunya is increasingly shaped by implementation and safety monitoring, while therapeutics remain limited. Fourth, competent vectors are being documented across a broader geographic range and are showing greater behavioral and ecological flexibility. Fifth, Aedes-focused vector control now has stronger evidence for reducing dengue risk, with Wolbachia replacement providing the clearest large-scale disease-endpoint evidence and several other approaches showing promising but more heterogeneous evidence. These five changes and their practical implications are summarized in Table 1. Figure 1 provides a complementary visual synthesis, positioning key developments along a continuum from public health challenges to opportunities, with mixed or evolving areas between them. Methods We conducted a narrative review of literature and public health guidance on arboviruses and their vectors published from January 1, 2020, through June 30, 2026. The review aimed to identify major developments since a prior 2020 overview, emphasizing findings relevant to clinicians, surveillance programs, vaccine and vector-control policy, and public health practice. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar using combinations of terms related to arboviruses, pathogens, vectors, surveillance, diagnostics, vaccines, therapeutics, and vector control. Search terms included combinations of “arbovirus”, “arthropod-borne virus”, “dengue”, “chikungunya”, “Zika”, “yellow fever”, “West Nile”, “Oropouche”, “Mayaro”, “Japanese encephalitis”, “Powassan”, “La Crosse”, “Aedes aegypti”, “Aedes albopictus”, “Culex”, “Culicoides”, “vector competence”, “range expansion”, “genomic surveillance”, “wastewater”, “environmental DNA”, “diagnostics”, “multiplex PCR”, “vaccine”, “therapeutic”, “Wolbachia”, “sterile insect technique”, “spatial repellent”, “pyriproxyfen”, and “indoor residual spraying”. Searches were supplemented by reference-list review and targeted review of surveillance, guidance, and regulatory documents from the World Health Organization, Pan American Health Organization, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and European Medicines Agency. We prioritized primary studies, clinical trials, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, major surveillance reports, policy recommendations, and regulatory documents that described substantial changes since 2020 or had direct implications for clinical care, surveillance, vaccination, therapeutics, vector ecology, or vector control. We excluded articles outside the 2020–2026 period unless needed for historical context, articles not directly relevant to human arboviral disease or vector-borne public health practice, studies focused only on basic virology or animal models without clear clinical or public health relevance, and duplicate or superseded guidance documents. Preprints were identified through Google Scholar, reference-list review, and coauthor expertise rather than a separate systematic search of preprint servers. They were considered only when they addressed rapidly evolving developments not yet represented in peer-reviewed literature and were identified as preprints in the reference list. One author (Z.J.M.) conducted the initial searches and screening. All coauthors reviewed selected evidence within their areas of expertise and suggested additional sources. Final inclusion was based on relevance to the five themes highlighted in this review and consensus among the authors. Because this was a narrative review rather than a systematic review or meta-analysis, we did not perform duplicate screening, formal risk-of-bias assessment, exhaustive evidence mapping, or pooled quantitative synthesis. Change 1: Dengue still dominates, but the resurgence and expansion of other arboviruses remain a threat Dengue remains the most widespread arboviral disease. In 2024, more than 14.4 million dengue cases, including over 52,000 severe cases and about 11,000 deaths, were reported globally—the highest annual totals in modern records and a major strain on health systems3. Dengue virus (DENV) serotype circulation has also shifted, with re-emergence of DENV-3 and increased detection of DENV-4 in parts of the Americas4,5. Genomic analyses suggest that many recent epidemics have been driven by overlapping lineages rather than by a single variant6,7. Intense dengue seasons therefore rarely have a single explanation. They can reflect the combined effects of co-circulating serotypes and lineages, changing population immunity, and ecological conditions that favor vector abundance. Immunologic studies have further clarified why some DENV infections progress to severe disease. Prior DENV infection is known to influence the risk of severe disease after subsequent infection. Newer work suggests that prior Zika virus (ZIKV) infection and qualitative features of the antibody response, including IgG afucosylation, may also shape risk8,9,10. Nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) also contributes to vascular leak and remains an important diagnostic target, reinforcing guidance to use NS1- or RNA-based tests early in illness when available11.
