Email: anikethreddygaddam@gmail.com ABSTRACT Background: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) is an acquired immune-mediated disorder characterized by isolated thrombocytopenia and increased bleeding risk. Dengue fever is a recognized trigger for secondary ITP. Case Presentation: A 42-year-old female presented with gum bleeding and oral purpura. She had a history of dengue fever three months earlier. Evaluation revealed severe thrombocytopenia, anemia, elevated LDH, and reactive lymphocytes. Autoimmune and infectious workup was negative. Management: The patient received corticosteroids, supportive transfusions, and symptomatic management. Secondary ITP following dengue infection was considered the most probable diagnosis. Conclusion: Persistent thrombocytopenia after dengue should prompt evaluation for secondary ITP. Keywords: Immune thrombocytopenia; Secondary ITP; Dengue fever; Thrombocytopenia; Autoimmune hematology; Corticosteroids; Post-infectious immune disorder. How to cite this article: Elavarasan, Subramaniam SK, Gnanaprakash, Arvindraj R, Gopinath A, Kishore MS, Gaddam AR. Beyond Dengue: Secondary Immune Thrombocytopenia Presenting as Persistent Mucocutaneous Bleeding-A Case Report and Narrative Review. Int J Drug Deliv Technol. 2026;16(57s): 1299-1301. DOI: 10.25258/ijddt.16.57s.128 Source of support: Nil Conflict of interest: None INTRODUCTION Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an acquired autoimmune disorder characterized by isolated thrombocytopenia resulting from increased platelet destruction and impaired platelet production. It may be primary or secondary to infections, autoimmune diseases, immunodeficiency states, and malignancies. Dengue fever is increasingly recognized as a trigger for persistent immune-mediated thrombocytopenia. This report describes a patient who developed probable secondary ITP following dengue infection and reviews current evidence regarding its epidemiology, pathogenesis, and management. CASE PRESENTATION A 42-year-old female presented with spontaneous bleeding from the gums for five days. She subsequently Beyond Dengue: Secondary Immune Thrombocytopenia Presenting as Persistent Mucocutaneous Bleeding-A Case Report and Narrative Review IJDDT, Volume 16 Issue 57s, 2026 Page 1300 developed multiple purpuric lesions over the oral mucosa. There was no history of hematuria, melena, menorrhagia, fever, rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, or recent drug intake. Three months prior, she had been diagnosed with dengue fever and received one unit of single donor platelets, four units of random donor platelets, and four units of fresh frozen plasma. Since recovery, she experienced intermittent gum bleeding and myalgias. On examination, pallor and oral purpura were present. There was no lymphadenopathy, edema, or hepatomegaly. Mild splenomegaly was noted. Laboratory investigations revealed: Hemoglobin: 6.1–7.2 g/dL Platelet count: 21,000–23,000/mm3 Total leukocyte count: Normal Peripheral smear: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with severe thrombocytopenia Reactive lymphocytes present LDH: 1040 U/L ANA profile: Negative Viral serology: Negative Direct Coombs test: Negative The patient received intravenous vitamin K, dexamethasone, pulse methylprednisolone, cefotaxime, proton pump inhibitor therapy, fresh frozen plasma, and packed red blood cell transfusion. Following exclusion of alternative etiologies, a diagnosis of probable secondary ITP following dengue infection was considered. NARRATIVE REVIEW Epidemiology and Clinical Presentation ITP affects approximately 2–5 individuals per 100,000 population annually. Secondary ITP accounts for nearly 20% of adult cases and may occur following viral infections including HIV, hepatitis C, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and dengue fever. Clinical manifestations range from asymptomatic thrombocytopenia to severe mucocutaneous bleeding. Common features include petechiae, purpura, ecchymosis, epistaxis, gingival bleeding, and menorrhagia. Severe internal bleeding is uncommon but may occur in profound thrombocytopenia Pathophysiological Mechanisms The pathogenesis of ITP involves both humoral and cellular immune dysfunction. Key mechanisms included are-Autoantibody-mediated platelet destruction,Splenic macrophage phagocytosis of antibody-coated platelets,T-cell-mediated platelet destruction,Impaired megakaryocyte maturation and platelet production,Persistent immune activation following infections such as dengue. Dengue-associated ITP is thought to result from molecular mimicry, immune complex formation, and prolonged immune dysregulation after viral clearance. Medical Management First-Line Therapy is corticosteroids,Prednisolone: 1–2 mg/kg/day and High-dose dexamethasone: 40 mg daily for 4 days Benefits are rapid platelet recovery, they are widely available and cost effective Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIg) Used when:Rapid platelet increase is required,severe bleeding occurs,steroids are contraindicated Second-line treatment options for ITP include rituximab, a monoclonal antibody directed against CD20-positive B lymphocytes that reduces autoantibody production through B-cell depletion; thrombopoietin receptor agonists such as romiplostim and eltrombopag, which stimulate platelet production and are particularly effective in chronic or refractory disease; and various immunosuppressive agents including azathioprine, cyclosporine, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclophosphamide, and dapsone. Splenectomy remains an important therapeutic option for patients with chronic ITP, steroid- dependent disease, refractory thrombocytopenia, or failure of medical therapy, providing durable remission in a substantial proportion of cases. Clinical significance Secondary ITP following dengue infection is uncommon but clinically important. Persistent thrombocytopenia after recovery from dengue should not automatically be attributed to residual viral effects. Early identification of immune-mediated mechanisms allows timely initiation of immunosuppressive therapy and prevention of bleeding complications. DISCUSSION This case highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by persistent thrombocytopenia following dengue infection. The temporal association with dengue, exclusion of autoimmune and malignant causes, and presence of reactive lymphocytes support an immune-mediated process. The favorable response to corticosteroid therapy further strengthens the diagnosis of secondary ITP. Early diagnosis is essential to prevent significant bleeding complications. CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for secondary ITP in patients with persistent Beyond Dengue: Secondary Immune Thrombocytopenia Presenting as Persistent Mucocutaneous Bleeding-A Case Report and Narrative Review IJDDT, Volume 16 Issue 57s, 2026 Page 1301 thrombocytopenia after dengue infection. Comprehensive evaluation and timely immunosuppressive therapy may reduce morbidity and improve patient outcomes. LIMITATIONS Bone marrow examination was not performed. Long-term follow-up data were unavailable because the patient opted for discharge against medical advice. A definitive causal relationship between dengue infection and ITP therefore cannot be conclusively established. Future Perspectives Further studies are required to determine the incidence, risk factors, and optimal management strategies for post- dengue ITP. Research into immunological biomarkers may facilitate earlier diagnosis and targeted therapy. CONCLUSION Secondary ITP should be considered in patients with persistent thrombocytopenia and bleeding manifestations following dengue infection. Prompt recognition, exclusion of alternative etiologies, and appropriate immunosuppressive therapy are critical for preventing complications and improving outcomes. REFERENCES 1. papers.title_original: Beyond Dengue: Secondary Immune Thrombocytopenia Presenting as Persistent Mucocutaneous Bleeding-A Case Report and Narrative Review

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on secondary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) presenting as persistent mucocutaneous bleeding, specifically in the context of dengue infection. The central question is whether persistent thrombocytopenia after dengue should be attributed to residual viral effects or an immune-mediated process.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative review and case report, not a systematic or meta-analysis. It includes a single case study of a patient with dengue infection who developed secondary ITP. The evidence is derived from clinical observations and laboratory findings, with no mention of databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria for study inclusion.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that secondary ITP following dengue infection is uncommon but clinically important. It emphasizes that persistent thrombocytopenia after dengue should not be automatically attributed to residual viral effects. The pathogenesis of ITP is described as involving immune dysfunction, including autoantibody-mediated platelet destruction, splenic macrophage phagocytosis, and T-cell-mediated destruction. The case supports an immune-mediated process rather than a direct viral effect.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that a definitive causal relationship between dengue infection and ITP cannot be conclusively established due to the lack of long-term follow-up data. It also highlights the need for further studies to determine the incidence, risk factors, and optimal management strategies for post-dengue ITP.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for secondary ITP in patients with persistent thrombocytopenia and bleeding manifestations following dengue infection. It recommends comprehensive evaluation and timely immunosuppressive therapy to reduce morbidity and improve patient outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review and case report explores secondary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) presenting as persistent mucocutaneous bleeding in the context of dengue infection. The review highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing between residual viral effects and immune-mediated processes in patients with prolonged thrombocytopenia. It concludes that secondary ITP is uncommon but clinically significant, and that persistent thrombocytopenia should not be automatically attributed to the virus. The case study supports an immune-mediated etiology, and the review emphasizes the need for further research on the incidence, risk factors, and management of post-dengue ITP. Clinicians are advised to consider secondary ITP in such cases and to pursue timely immunosuppressive therapy.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注表现为持续性皮肤粘膜出血的继发性免疫性血小板减少症(ITP),特别是在登革热感染的情况下。核心问题是登革热后持续性血小板减少是否应归因于残留病毒效应或免疫介导的过程。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论是叙述性评论和病例报告,而不是系统分析或荟萃分析。它包括一名患有登革热感染并出现继发性 ITP 的患者的单个案例研究。证据来自临床观察和实验室结果,没有提及数据库、检索日期或研究纳入的资格标准。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,登革热感染后继发性 ITP 并不常见,但具有临床意义。它强调登革热后持续性血小板减少不应自动归因于残留病毒效应。ITP 的 发病机制 被描述为涉及免疫功能障碍,包括自身抗体介导的血小板破坏、脾巨噬细胞吞噬作用和 T 细胞介导的破坏。该病例支持免疫介导的过程,而不是直接的病毒效应。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查指出,由于缺乏长期随访数据,无法最终确定登革热感染与 ITP 之间的明确因果关系。它还强调需要进一步研究以确定登革热后 ITP 的 发病率、风险因素和最佳管理策略。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述建议,对于登革热感染后出现持续性血小板减少和出血表现的患者,临床医生应对继发性 ITP 保持高度怀疑。它建议进行全面评估并及时进行免疫抑制治疗,以降低发病率并改善患者预后。

papers.abstract: Sốt xuất huyết Dengue (SXHD) là bệnh truyền nhiễm lưu hành ở mức cao tại tỉnh Khánh Hòa trong nhiềunăm. Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang hồi cứu được thực hiện nhằm mô tả sự thay đổi đặc điểm dịch tễ họcSXHD tại Khánh Hòa giai đoạn 2018-2024. Phân tích mô tả kết hợp phân tích chuỗi thời gian ngắt quãng(Interrupted Time Series Analysis) được sử dụng để đánh giá xu hướng biến động số ca mắc theo thờigian. Giai đoạn nghiên cứu có tổng cộng 45.828 trường hợp mắc SXHD và 11 trường hợp tử vong doSXHD. Bệnh xuất hiện quanh năm, với xu hướng gia tăng vào các tháng cuối năm; đỉnh dịch lớn nhấtđược ghi nhận vào tháng 11 năm 2020 với 2.397 trường hợp mắc/tháng. analysis.research_question_and_background: Nghiên cứu được thực hiện nhằm mô tả sự thay đổi đặc điểm dịch tễ học của bệnh sốt xuất huyết dengue tại Khánh Hòa giai đoạn 2018-2024, do bệnh này là một dịch bệnh truyền nhiễm lưu hành ở mức cao tại tỉnh trong nhiều năm.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang hồi cứu được thực hiện tại Khánh Hòa, Việt Nam, từ năm 2018 đến 2024, bao gồm tổng cộng 45.828 trường hợp mắc sốt xuất huyết dengue và 11 trường hợp tử vong do bệnh này.
analysis.methods: Phân tích mô tả kết hợp phân tích chuỗi thời gian ngắt quãng (Interrupted Time Series Analysis) được sử dụng để đánh giá xu hướng biến động số ca mắc theo thời gian.
analysis.main_results: Giai đoạn nghiên cứu ghi nhận bệnh SXHD xuất hiện quanh năm, với xu hướng gia tăng vào các tháng cuối năm; đỉnh dịch lớn nhất được ghi nhận vào tháng 11 năm 2020 với 2.397 trường hợp mắc/tháng.

analysis.summary_en: This study describes the epidemiological changes of dengue in Khanh Hoa province from 2018 to 2024, highlighting a significant increase in cases during the last months of the year, with the highest outbreak recorded in November 2020. The research used a cross-sectional retrospective design combined with interrupted time series analysis to evaluate trends in dengue incidence over time. The findings indicate that dengue remains a prevalent infectious disease in the region, with seasonal variations and a notable peak in 2020. The study suggests the importance of monitoring and adjusting disease control measures according to seasonal patterns. However, the research is limited by its reliance on reported data and lack of detailed causal analysis, resulting in moderate confidence in the evidence.

papers.full_text: Evaluating the Efficacy of Serodiagnosis Technique of Dengue Virus Infection: An Epidemiological Study and Surveillance Analysis in Dimapur, Nagaland, India Abstract: This study assessed the serodiagnostic and epidemiological characteristics of dengue virus (DENV) infection in Dimapur, Nagaland, India. A prospective study was conducted at the Department of Microbiology, District Hospital, Dimapur, from March 2023 to February 2024. Serum samples from 7,074 patients with suspected dengue infection were screened using rapid diagnostic tests for NS1 antigen and IgM antibodies, followed by NS1 and IgM ELISA confirmation. Selected samples were analyzed by RT-PCR for DENV serotyping. ELISA confirmed dengue infection in 2,010 cases, including 1,461 NS1-positive and 549 IgM-positive samples. Cases increased during the post-monsoon period, with the highest number recorded in October. Infection was more common among males and was most frequent in individuals aged 21-30 years. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of serodiagnosis techniques for dengue virus infection and assess its epidemiological characteristics in Dimapur, Nagaland, India, to inform public health strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective study was conducted at the Department of Microbiology, District Hospital, Dimapur, from March 2023 to February 2024, involving 7,074 patients with suspected dengue infection.
analysis.methods: Serum samples were screened using rapid diagnostic tests for NS1 antigen and IgM antibodies, followed by NS1 and IgM ELISA confirmation. Selected samples were analyzed by RT-PCR for DENV serotyping.
analysis.main_results: ELISA confirmed dengue infection in 2,010 cases, including 1,461 NS1-positive and 549 IgM-positive samples. Among 39 samples suitable for molecular analysis, DENV-2 was detected in 13 samples, while 10 demonstrated co-infection with DENV-1 and DENV-2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the seasonal and demographic variation in dengue transmission and the circulation of multiple DENV serotypes, providing novel insights into the epidemiological patterns of the disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the importance of timely serological diagnosis and molecular surveillance, particularly during the post-monsoon season, to enhance dengue prevention and control efforts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are based on a single center and a specific time period, which may limit generalizability. However, the evidence is strong due to the use of multiple diagnostic methods and the detailed epidemiological analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the serodiagnosis technique for dengue virus infection in Dimapur, Nagaland, India, through a prospective epidemiological study conducted from March 2023 to February 2024. Serum samples from 7,074 suspected dengue patients were tested using rapid diagnostic tests for NS1 antigen and IgM antibodies, followed by ELISA confirmation and RT-PCR for serotyping. The results showed that ELISA confirmed 2,010 cases, with DENV-2 detected in 13 samples and co-infection with DENV-1 and DENV-2 in 10 samples. The study identified seasonal and demographic variations in dengue transmission, with the highest cases recorded in October. It also noted that infection was more common among males and individuals aged 21-30 years. The findings suggest the need for strengthening timely serological diagnosis and molecular surveillance, especially during the post-monsoon season, to improve dengue prevention and control. The study's limitations include its focus on a single center and time period, which may affect generalizability, but the evidence is robust due to the use of multiple diagnostic methods and detailed epidemiological analysis.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估印度那加兰邦迪马普尔 登革病毒 感染血清诊断技术的有效性,并评估其流行病学特征,为公共卫生策略提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2023年3月至2024年2月,迪马普尔地区医院微生物科进行了一项前瞻性研究,涉及7,074名疑似登革热感染患者。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 NS1 抗原和 IgM 抗体快速诊断测试筛选血清样本,然后进行 NS1 和 IgM ELISA 确认。通过 RT-PCR 对所选样本进行 DENV 血清分型分析。
elements_zh.main_results: ELISA 确诊 2,010 例登革热感染病例,其中 1,461 例 NS1 阳性样本和 549 例 IgM 阳性样本。在39个适合分子分析的样本中,有13个样本检测到DENV-2,而10个样本则证明DENV-1和DENV-2同时感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调了登革热 传播 的季节性和人口统计变化以及多种 DENV 血清型的传播,为该疾病的流行病学模式提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了及时进行血清学 诊断 和分子 监测 检测对于加强登革热预防和控制工作的重要性,特别是在季风后季节。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于单一中心和特定时间段,这可能会限制普遍性。然而,由于使用了多种诊断方法和详细的流行病学分析,证据是强有力的。

papers.full_text: ABSTRACTThe Amapa State, Brazil, in the Amazon region and bordering French Guiana, is a strategic sentinel location for infectious disease surveillance. Ecological pressures such as deforestation, artisanal gold mining, and high human mobility contribute to complex transmission dynamics of arboviruses, bacterial infections, and other pathogens. This study aims to characterize the etiologies of acute febrile illness (AFI) reported in Amapa State in 2018-2020, focusing on arbovirus circulation, bacterial contributions, and emerging pathogens. A retrospective analysis was carried out with 727 AFI cases. Laboratory diagnoses were established using molecular and serological assays, with systematic testing for different pathogens. Definitive diagnoses were obtained in 185 individuals (25.4%), yielding 209 positive results and including 23 cases of co-infection. Dengue virus was the predominant etiological agent (n=109, 52%), followed by leptospirosis (n=20, 9.5%), chikungunya virus (n=16, 7.6%), parvovirus B19 (n=16, 7.6%), measles (n=15, 7.1%), zika virus (n=10, 4.8%), mayaro virus (n=1,0.5%), and other bacterial infections (n=5, 2.4%). Isolated cases of hepatitis A and B, malaria, SARS-CoV-2, enterovirus, and acute Chagas disease were also identified. No hepatitis E virus or oropouche cases were detected. Dengue virus was the leading cause of AFI. Leptospirosis, chikungunya virus, and parvovirus B19 were other prevalent and often underrecognized contributors. The detection of additional viruses highlights Amapa State as a potential zone of “silent expansion” for emerging arboviruses. Co-detection of multiple pathogens underscores diagnostic complexity in regions with overlapping transmission. Strengthening surveillance, expanding laboratory capacity, and prioritizing differential diagnostics are essential to capture epidemiological dynamics and guide public health interventions.KEYWORDS: Dengue, Leptospirosis, Arbovirus infections, Chikungunya fever, Parvovirus B19 MATERIAL AND METHODSStudy design and populationAn observational, cross-sectional, retrospective, and descriptive study was conducted using a convenience sample. Serum specimens were collected from patients presenting with AFI during routine diagnostic procedures in public health laboratories. Samples from 727 individuals, collected in 2018 (n = 20), 2019 (n = 581), and 2020 (n = 126), were analyzed.This study aims to find the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in AFI cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion.Laboratory proceduresSpecimens were initially processed at the Central Public Health Laboratory of Amapa State (LACEN-AP) following routine diagnostic protocols, including arbovirus screening when clinically indicated. Additional tests, such as serology and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for other pathogens, were performed at the discretion of attending physicians, with results recorded on GAL. Confirmatory local methods included enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and NS1 (the latter exclusively for dengue), electrochemiluminescence, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), and sequencing; for bacterial and fungal infections, ELISA for leptospirosis and blood, urine, and stool cultures were performed; whereas parasitic infections were confirmed using thick blood smears, the Strout test, electrochemiluminescence, and immunochromatographic tests.After initial processing, samples were stored at −20 °C and shipped to the Virology Laboratory of the Institute of Tropical Medicine of Sao Paulo, Faculty of Medicine, University of Sao Paulo (LV-IMT-FMUSP, LIM-52), in which they were preserved at −80 °C until further testing.Molecular screeningAt LV-IMT-FMUSP, samples underwent real-time PCR assays targeting viral agents. The screening included assays for Pan-Orthoflavivirus and Pan-Alphavirus. The following viral agents were tested: Flaviviruses, Alphaviruses, Orthobunyaviruses: yellow fever 8 , dengue, zika, chikungunya, mayaro, and oropouche viruses 9 .Genus Orthoflavivirus 10 : Japanese encephalitis, Russian spring-summer encephalitis, tick-borne encephalitis, Usutu, West Nile, and Saint Louis encephalitis viruses.Genus Alphavirus 11 : Ross River, O’nyong-nyong, Sindbis, Barmah Forest, Eastern equine encephalitis, Western equine encephalitis, and Venezuelan equine encephalitis viruses. Additional real-time PCR assays included pathogens with overlapping clinical presentations, such as enterovirus 12 , parvovirus B19 13 , hepatitis E virus (HEV) 14 , and Leptospira spp 15 .GALIn this study, diagnostic test results from LACEN-AP were retrieved via GAL.GAL, the national computerized system, was designed to manage and monitor laboratory routines within the National Public Health Laboratory Network. It is managed by the Ministry of Health via the General Coordination of Public Health Laboratories and tracks the flow of biological samples from collection to final diagnosis, standardizing results and providing real-time data for the surveillance of high-priority and compulsory notification diseases.SINANSINAN, the primary national surveillance database managed by the Brazilian Ministry of Health, is a decentralized system fed by the mandatory notification of diseases and conditions in the National Compulsory Notification List.SINAN provides high-resolution microdata (individual-level records) that include clinical and demographic variables (age, sex, pregnancy status, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations), diagnostic test results, among others.Integration of dataClinical and demographic variables (age, sex, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations) were combined with GAL laboratory results. Using this integrated dataset, data analysis was strictly descriptive, focusing on characterizing the reported cases.For the diagnostic tests either at LACEN or IMT, samples were classified as positive if they were reactive in at least one assay.Statistical analysisContinuous variables are shown as medians and interquartile ranges (IQR), and categorical ones, as frequencies. Subgroup pairwise comparisons were performed via the Pearson’s chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. Correlation between monthly cases and NASA POWER precipitation data was assessed using Spearman’s rank test. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate across multiple comparisons. Spatial distribution maps were generated using the geobr, sf, and ggplot2 packages. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05, using R(version 4.4.0) via RStudio. Study design and populationAn observational, cross-sectional, retrospective, and descriptive study was conducted using a convenience sample. Serum specimens were collected from patients presenting with AFI during routine diagnostic procedures in public health laboratories. Samples from 727 individuals, collected in 2018 (n = 20), 2019 (n = 581), and 2020 (n = 126), were analyzed.This study aims to find the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in AFI cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil. AFI, with a fever duration cutoff of 2-7 day from onset, was chosen as the inclusion criterion. Regarding age, the female sex presented a median age of 28 years (interquartile range : 15-45), with values ranging from0.008 to 90 years. For males, the median age was 26 years (IQR: 12-42), ranging from 0.17 to 88 years. full_text_sections.discussion: DISCUSSIONThis study investigated the etiologies of AFI cases reported in Amapa State from 2018 to 2022. Of 727 evaluated individuals, definitive diagnoses established 185 cases (25.4%), including 23 cases of co-infection.Our findings are in line with previous regional studies. Dengue remains the predominant AFI etiological agent in Latin America, with chikungunya and zika showing an increased prevalence. Leptospirosis, though often overlooked, represents a prevalent bacterial contributor1,16.Notably, this study found one case of mayaro virus infection, consistent with its rare occurrence in Amapa State (six confirmed cases nationwide in 2015-2025) 17 . Following systematic PCR testing, no individual in our cohort was positive for Oropouche virus disease, despite epidemiological data (2015-2025) reporting 16,571 cases nationwide, including 218 in Amapa State. A recent increase in its detection (2023-2024) likely reflects greater diagnostic capacity and active case-finding 17 . These results suggest Amapa State may represent a zone of “silent expansion” for Oropouche virus disease, in which overlapping arbovirus transmission obscures true disease burden. Strengthening surveillance, expanding laboratory capacity, and prioritizing differential diagnostics are essential to capture epidemiological dynamics and guide interventions. While multiplex syndromic panels are ideal, widespread molecular testing faces strict budget and logistical constraints within the public health system in Amapa State. A more sustainable solution could be a tiered “reflex testing” cascade at LACEN-AP. Under this protocol, a negative molecular result for primary arboviruses (dengue/zika/chikungunya) would automatically trigger reflex testing for leptospirosis and parvovirus B19 using the original biological sample. This flow could optimize laboratory resources, cut costs, and bypass initial clinical triage blind spots without requiring secondary patient appointments. Lessons from the Amazon highlight the global importance of integrated arbovirus surveillance in regions with overlapping transmission.The fact that 80.5% of initial hypotheses were generically classified as suspected arboviruses exposes a profound “dengue-centric” bias. Because the early symptoms of dengue, parvovirus B19, and leptospirosis overlap almost entirely, physical triage alone is insufficient. To address this, the regional health system must implement targeted continuing medical education focusing on broad syndromic classifications—such as “acute exanthematous febrile syndrome”—rather than single-pathogen guessing. Furthermore, standard patient intake forms should mandate structured epidemiological risk questions regarding recent floodwater exposure (leptospirosis), mining or forest exposure (malaria/arboviruses), and artisanal acai consumption (acute Chagas disease) to guide clinical suspicion before laboratory results are available.Leptospirosis remains a critical public health challenge in Amapa State linked to seasonal flooding, precarious sanitation, and transmission in wetland and stilt-house communities 18 , 19 . Despite its prevalence, underreporting persists due to symptomatic overlap with malaria and dengue 20 . Our finding that Leptospira spp. was the second most prevalent confirmed pathogen underscores its critical standing in the regional etiology of AFI. Unlike arboviral infections, which only require supportive care, leptospirosis demands timely antibiotic therapy to prevent severe, potentially fatal complications such as Weil’s disease or pulmonary hemorrhage syndrome. Relying entirely on early clinical differentiation or waiting days for laboratory confirmation in highly endemic zones often results in catastrophic therapeutic delays. Therefore, in areas with high dengue and leptospirosis co-endemicity, clinical protocols must explicitly support the initiation of empirical antibiotic treatment (such as doxycycline or amoxicillin) for patients presenting with severe febrile syndromes and clear epidemiological risk factors, prioritizing clinical survival over definitive laboratory timelines.Parvovirus B19 occurred in 16 cases (7.6%), representing a notable proportion of AFI diagnoses. Its clinical recognition remains challenging as its early symptoms closely mimic arboviruses such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. In tropical regions, B19V is often misdiagnosed as dengue due to overlapping presentations of fever, headache, and rash 21 , 22 . The post-pandemic resurgence of B19V in 2024-2025 marked a significant epidemiological shift driven by an “immunity gap” in pediatric populations. IgM positivity peaked at ~40% in children aged 5-9 years and ~10% in adults, complicating AFI differential diagnosis 23 .Of the 727 investigated individuals, viral hepatitis was suspected in 10 cases (1.4%), with three confirmed cases of hepatitis A and B (1.4%). No HEV cases were identified despite evidence that HEV genotype 3 is a zoonotic pathogen of concern in Brazil 24 , 25 .Meta-analyses estimate anti-HEV IgG seroprevalence at ~6% nationally, with regional variations: ~3% in the Amazon and up to 14.2% in rural Rondônia 26 - 28 . Diagnostic invisibility remains a major challenge as public health screening routinely ignores HEV testing, particularly in vulnerable Amazonian populations. Overlapping clinical presentations with hepatitis b and d further obscure HEV detection, suggesting that some acute hepatitis cases of “unknown etiology” may represent undiagnosed HEV.Measles occurred in 15 cases (7.1%). Despite mass vaccination programs, Brazil lost its measles-free status in 2018 following outbreaks linked to Venezuelan migration and low vaccination coverage 29 , 30 . Although elimination status was regained in 2023-2024, new cases in Tocantins in 2025 highlight ongoing vulnerability. The porous border of Amapa State with French Guiana and high mobility of illegal gold miners create a unique epidemiological corridor sustaining measles and other infectious diseases.Malaria transmission remains a major concern in Oiapoque, one of the highest transmission zones in the Americas. Despite persistent “silent” transmission by asymptomatic carriers in mobile populations, our cohort only included two malaria cases (0.95%), reflecting the predominance of samples collected in Macapa. Epidemiological data shows a downward trend in Amapa State, with a 16.8% reduction in cases from 2024 to 2025 and an 82% decline in Macapa. Nonetheless, the Oiapoque border remains the main epidemiological challenge in the state 31 - 34 . The cohort included a case of acute Chagas disease, reflecting the specific epidemiological profile of Amapa State. From 2018 to 2022, the state remained a high-endemicity region for acute Chagas disease in the Brazilian Amazon, with oral transmission—primarily by consumption of artisanal acai and bacaba juice—emerging as the dominant route of infection 35 , 36 .A notable finding in this study was the elevated detection of multiple infectious agents. Across 727 patients, this study found 209 reactive results, with co-detection of distinct pathogens in 23 cases. Similar patterns have been reported in regions endemic for malaria and arboviruses, in which simultaneous infections are confirmed by multiple molecular assays 37 , 38 . In such contexts, potential cross-reactivity further compounds diagnostic complexity. The cross-reactivity between zika, dengue, and yellow fever serological assays, for example, is primarily attributed to the high degree of structural homology within the envelope protein in members of the Orthoflavivirus genus 39 .The seasonal transmission pattern in this study likely reflects the equatorial climate of the region, in which persistently high precipitation and elevated temperatures sustain vector breeding sites throughout the year. full_text_sections.conclusion: CONCLUSIONSThe causes of AFI in Amapa are multiple and may involve infection by more than one etiological agent. This underscores the complexity of diagnostic accuracy in regions with overlapping multiple arbovirus and bacterial transmission. The detection of rare pathogens such as Mayaro virus and acute Chagas disease reflects the unique ecological and epidemiological profile of the region. These findings reinforce the role of Amapa State as a sentinel for infectious disease surveillance as its porous borders, ecological connectivity, and high human mobility sustain transmission corridors. Strengthening laboratory capacity, integrating differential diagnostics, and expanding surveillance systems are essential to capture the true burden of AFI and to guide targeted interventions. While acknowledging the limitations inherent to retrospective designs and diagnostic constraints, this study emphasizes the global relevance of integrated surveillance in ecologically dynamic regions. Crucially, addressing these challenges requires improving data completeness, such as by the meticulous entry and digital optimization of GAL forms, to ensure accurate epidemiological tracking in complex equatorial settings.
full_text_sections.other: INTRODUCTIONManaging the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of community-acquired acute febrile illness (AFI) constitutes a major public health challenge in Latin America due to its complex epidemiological profile and potentially profound social consequences 1 . A comprehensive understanding of their etiologies is essential for advancing clinical practice, guiding public health strategies, and informing policy development.The ecology of the Amazon basin—characterized by deforestation, flooding, and high vector diversity—creates favorable conditions for arboviruses and bacterial pathogens, amplifying the risk of febrile outbreaks 2 . Thus, the region experiences a wide spectrum of febrile illnesses caused by viral, bacterial, and parasitic agents, reflecting diverse ecological and climatic conditions 3 .The overlapping clinical manifestations of diseases such as dengue, malaria, leptospirosis, and rickettsial infections complicate accurate diagnosis. This diagnostic uncertainty often results in delayed or inappropriate treatment. Misdiagnosis may postpone life-saving antibiotic therapy, whereas indiscriminate prescribing contributes to antimicrobial resistance. The Pan American Health Organization 4 has emphasized antimicrobial resistance as a regional priority, highlighting its impact on healthcare costs and mortality.Community-acquired AFI contributes substantially to regional morbidity and mortality, considerably straining healthcare systems and requiring significant resource allocation for surveillance and management. Socioeconomic factors, including poverty and limited access to healthcare, exacerbate transmission dynamics and hinder effective disease control 5 .Surveillance represents a critical component of disease control. The Brazilian Amazon is recognized as a global hotspot for emerging viruses 2 . Integrated screening systems may serve as sentinel mechanisms for early detection. As deforestation and mining activities intensify, human populations increasingly encounter novel vectors such as mosquitoes and midges, underscoring the importance of screening febrile patients for malaria and arboviruses6. Without routine screening, outbreaks may remain undetected, manifesting themselves only as “unexplained fevers.”Amapa State, in the Eastern Brazilian Amazon, exemplifies one of the most complex diagnostic environments in the world. While dengue remains a major concern, the unique geography of the state—bordering French Guiana and the Atlantic Ocean, and dominated by dense rainforest and wetlands—heightens the risk of diverse infectious diseases. High rainfall and humidity render leptospirosis endemic, particularly in peri-urban areas such as Macapa and Santana 5 . Recent land-use transformations, including illegal mining and the expansion of acai production, have had measurable epidemiological consequences. These activities are consistently associated with increased malaria incidence due to favorable conditions for Anopheles vectors 6 . Moreover, the commercialization of acai has contributed to the emergence of foodborne transmission of Chagas disease 7 .EthicsThis study was approved by the institutional Research Ethics Committee (CAAE No 53153916.7.0000.0065). All data were anonymized prior to analysis, and access to secondary data from the Laboratory Environment Manager (GAL) and the Notifiable Diseases Information System (SINAN) was restricted to variables necessary for epidemiological characterization (with authorization from health surveillance authorities). EthicsThis study was approved by the institutional Research Ethics Committee (CAAE No 53153916.7.0000.0065). All data were anonymized prior to analysis, and access to secondary data from the Laboratory Environment Manager (GAL) and the Notifiable Diseases Information System (SINAN) was restricted to variables necessary for epidemiological characterization (with authorization from health surveillance authorities). Laboratory proceduresSpecimens were initially processed at the Central Public Health Laboratory of Amapa State (LACEN-AP) following routine diagnostic protocols, including arbovirus screening when clinically indicated. Additional tests, such as serology and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for other pathogens, were performed at the discretion of attending physicians, with results recorded on GAL. Confirmatory local methods included enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and NS1 (the latter exclusively for dengue), electrochemiluminescence, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), and sequencing; for bacterial and fungal infections, ELISA for leptospirosis and blood, urine, and stool cultures were performed; whereas parasitic infections were confirmed using thick blood smears, the Strout test, electrochemiluminescence, and immunochromatographic tests.After initial processing, samples were stored at −20 °C and shipped to the Virology Laboratory of the Institute of Tropical Medicine of Sao Paulo, Faculty of Medicine, University of Sao Paulo (LV-IMT-FMUSP, LIM-52), in which they were preserved at −80 °C until further testing. Molecular screeningAt LV-IMT-FMUSP, samples underwent real-time PCR assays targeting viral agents. The screening included assays for Pan-Orthoflavivirus and Pan-Alphavirus. The following viral agents were tested: Flaviviruses, Alphaviruses, Orthobunyaviruses: yellow fever 8 , dengue, zika, chikungunya, mayaro, and oropouche viruses 9 .Genus Orthoflavivirus 10 : Japanese encephalitis, Russian spring-summer encephalitis, tick-borne encephalitis, Usutu, West Nile, and Saint Louis encephalitis viruses.Genus Alphavirus 11 : Ross River, O’nyong-nyong, Sindbis, Barmah Forest, Eastern equine encephalitis, Western equine encephalitis, and Venezuelan equine encephalitis viruses. Additional real-time PCR assays included pathogens with overlapping clinical presentations, such as enterovirus 12 , parvovirus B19 13 , hepatitis E virus (HEV) 14 , and Leptospira spp 15 . GALIn this study, diagnostic test results from LACEN-AP were retrieved via GAL.GAL, the national computerized system, was designed to manage and monitor laboratory routines within the National Public Health Laboratory Network. It is managed by the Ministry of Health via the General Coordination of Public Health Laboratories and tracks the flow of biological samples from collection to final diagnosis, standardizing results and providing real-time data for the surveillance of high-priority and compulsory notification diseases. SINANSINAN, the primary national surveillance database managed by the Brazilian Ministry of Health, is a decentralized system fed by the mandatory notification of diseases and conditions in the National Compulsory Notification List.SINAN provides high-resolution microdata (individual-level records) that include clinical and demographic variables (age, sex, pregnancy status, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations), diagnostic test results, among others. Integration of dataClinical and demographic variables (age, sex, municipality of residence, reported condition, date of symptom onset, and clinical manifestations) were combined with GAL laboratory results. Using this integrated dataset, data analysis was strictly descriptive, focusing on characterizing the reported cases.For the diagnostic tests either at LACEN or IMT, samples were classified as positive if they were reactive in at least one assay. Subgroup pairwise comparisons were performed via the Pearson’s chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. papers.title_original: Sentinel surveillance of acute febrile illness in a Brazilian Amazon region: laboratory findings and epidemiological implications

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify the potential etiologies of viral and other infections in acute febrile illness (AFI) cases reported from 2018 to 2022 in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil, to better understand the epidemiological landscape of infectious diseases in the area.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a sentinel surveillance conducted in public health laboratories in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil, from 2018 to 2022. A total of 727 individuals were evaluated, with definitive diagnoses established in 185 cases (25.4%), including 23 cases of co-infection.
analysis.methods: Diagnostic tests included enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for immunoglobulin M (IgM) and NS1, electrochemiluminescence, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR), and sequencing. Samples were stored at −20 °C and shipped to the Virology Laboratory of the Institute of Tropical Medicine of Sao Paulo (LV-IMT-FMUSP) for further testing, where real-time PCR assays were performed to identify viral agents.
analysis.main_results: Dengue virus was the most frequent diagnosis, accounting for 109 cases (16.8%) out of 650 tests. Other notable findings included leptospirosis (20/98; 20.4%), chikungunya (16/86; 18.6%), and measles (15/53; 28.3%). Non-dengue positive cases included Zika (9/62; 14.5%), parvovirus B19 (6/21; 28.6%), and bacterial infections (5/17; 29.4%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as highlighting the significant role of dengue virus in the etiology of AFI in the region, with notable co-infections observed. This study provides novel insights into the distribution and prevalence of dengue and other pathogens in the Amazon region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies for dengue and other co-infecting pathogens in the Amazon region, aiding in the development of more effective public health interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's descriptive analysis may limit the depth of interpretation, and the use of multiple diagnostic methods could introduce variability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and the potential for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted sentinel surveillance of acute febrile illness (AFI) in the Amazon region of Amapa State, Brazil, from 2018 to 2022 to identify potential etiologies. Dengue virus was the most frequent diagnosis, accounting for 16.8% of cases, followed by leptospirosis, chikungunya, and measles. The study used a combination of serology, PCR, and sequencing methods to confirm diagnoses, with 209 positive results across 185 individuals. Co-infections were observed in 23 cases, and the results showed a moderate positive correlation with rainfall. The study's descriptive nature and reliance on multiple diagnostic methods limit the depth of interpretation, resulting in moderate evidence strength. These findings can inform targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies for dengue and other pathogens in the region.

This study provides novel insights into the distribution and prevalence of dengue and other pathogens in the Amazon region.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies for dengue and other co-infecting pathogens in the Amazon region, aiding in the development of more effective public health interventions.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's descriptive analysis may limit the depth of interpretation, and the use of multiple diagnostic methods could introduce variability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and the potential for confounding factors.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在确定2018年至2022年巴西阿马帕州亚马逊地区报告的急性发热性疾病(AFI)病例中病毒和其他感染的潜在病因,以更好地了解该地区传染病的流行病学状况。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是2018年至2022年在巴西阿马帕州亚马逊地区公共卫生实验室进行的前哨监测研究。共评估了727人,确诊185例(25.4%),其中23例合并感染。
analysis_zh.methods: 诊断测试包括免疫球蛋白 M (IgM) 和 NS1 的酶联免疫吸附测定 (ELISA)、电化学发光、逆转录 PCR (RT-PCR) 和测序。样本储存在-20°C,并运送到圣保罗热带医学研究所(LV-IMT-FMUSP)病毒学实验室进行进一步测试,在那里进行实时PCR检测以鉴定病毒因子。
analysis_zh.main_results: 登革病毒 是最常见的 诊断,在 650 次测试中占 109 例(16.8%)。其他值得注意的发现包括钩端螺旋体病(20/98;20.4%)、基孔肯雅热(16/86;18.6%)和麻疹(15/53;28.3%)。非登革热阳性病例包括寨卡病毒(9/62;14.5%)、细小病毒B19(6/21;28.6%)和细菌感染(5/17;29.4%)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为强调了 登革病毒 在该地区 AFI 病因学中的重要作用,并观察到了显着的合并感染。这项研究为亚马逊地区登革热和其他病原体的分布和 患病率 提供了新的见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为亚马逊地区登革热和其他共感染病原体的针对性 监测 和诊断策略提供信息,有助于制定更有效的公共卫生干预措施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的描述性分析可能会限制解释的深度,并且多种诊断方法的使用可能会引入变异性。由于研究的观察性质和潜在的混杂因素,证据的强度适中。

papers.title: Prévention de la dengue à Wassakara : enquête sur les connaissances, attitudes et pratiques, Yopougon-Est, Côte d’Ivoire, 2025
papers.abstract: Introduction : La dengue est une maladie infectieuse transmise par des moustiques et qui connaît une forte croissance en Afrique de l’Ouest, notamment en Côte d’Ivoire. Malgré les efforts des institutions sanitaires, la maladie reste sous-diagnostiquée et difficile à contrôler, particulièrement dans les zones urbaines et périurbaines comme Abidjan. Cette étude s’est focalisée sur Wassakara, un quartier défavorisé de la commune de Yopougon à Abidjan, afin d’évaluer les connaissances, attitudes et pratiques (CAP) des adultes concernant la prévention contre la dengue. Méthode : Une enquête transversale a été menée auprès de 316 adultes sélectionnés aléatoirement. Un questionnaire structuré a permis de recueillir des données sociodémographiques et le niveau de CAP. Les analyses statistiques ont inclus des tests du khi-deux et des régressions logistiques pour identifier les facteurs influents. Résultats : Si la majorité (94,3 %) connaît l’existence de la dengue, les connaissances spécifiques sur sa transmission, ses symptômes et la prévention sont insuffisantes : seuls 7,6 % ont obtenu un score de connaissances satisfaisant, et à peine 2,8 % adoptaient régulièrement des pratiques protectrices. La mobilisation lors des campagnes de salubrité était faible. Les facteurs associés à de meilleurs scores sont l’âge, le niveau d’éducation, la taille du ménage et l’engagement collectif. Conclusion : L’étude conclut à la nécessité d’intensifier les actions ciblées d’éducation sanitaire, la formation des agents communautaires et la fourniture de moyens adaptés. Une stratégie multisectorielle et participative est indispensable pour renforcer la résilience communautaire.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted in Wassakara, a disadvantaged neighborhood in Yopougon, Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (CAP) of adults regarding dengue prevention. A cross-sectional survey of 316 randomly selected adults revealed that while most were aware of dengue, their specific knowledge about transmission, symptoms, and prevention was limited, with only 7.6% achieving a satisfactory knowledge score and 2.8% regularly adopting protective practices. The analyses identified age, education level, household size, and collective engagement as factors associated with better CAP scores. The authors emphasized the need for targeted health education, community agent training, and resource provision to improve dengue prevention. They also called for a multi-sectoral and participatory strategy to enhance community resilience. The study highlights the importance of addressing knowledge gaps and mobilizing communities in dengue control efforts, but its reliance on self-reported data and cross-sectional design limits the depth and generalizability of its findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热是一种传染病,在西非传播,并在科特迪瓦传播。卫生机构的努力,以及阿比让城市和周边地区的疾病诊断和控制困难。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究重点是瓦萨卡拉,阿比让约普贡社区的一个偏爱地区,旨在评估有关预防登革热的成年人的知识、态度和实践 (CAP)。共有 316 个成人选项可供选择。
elements_zh.methods: 联合国调查问卷结构允许社会人口统计和认识、态度和实践 (CAP) 的恢复。统计分析包括双因素测试和影响因素识别的逻辑回归。

papers.title: Arbovirus diagnostics: from conventional methods to emerging technologies—a chikungunya virus-centric review
papers.abstract: Arboviruses remain an important global health concern because of their expanding distribution, diverse transmission patterns, and the challenges associated with accurate and timely diagnosis. This review is centered on Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) as a representative model, focusing on diagnostic strategies across different stages of infection and the key diagnostic pitfalls that affect CHIKV detection in co-circulation settings. In this review, we summarize current laboratory-based approaches for CHIKV detection and differential diagnosis, including virus isolation, antigen detection, nucleic acid amplification and serological assays, with discussion of their applications, strengths and limitations. We further review recent developments in emerging diagnostic technologies, including next-generation sequencing, CRISPR-based detection methods, aptamer-based recognition systems, biosensors, and point-of-care testing platforms, highlighting their potential advantages and current limitations. Comparative examples involving dengue virus (DENV) and Zika virus (ZIKV) are discussed specifically to illustrate cross-reactivity and misclassification risks relevant to CHIKV diagnosis. Particular attention is given to persistent issues affecting diagnostic accuracy and practical implementation, including serological cross-reactivity among co-circulating arboviruses and the challenges of translating advanced technologies into accessible tools for field and resource-limited settings. Overall, this review summarizes progress in CHIKV-relevant diagnostics and outlines future opportunities for developing more reliable, rapid, and widely applicable detection strategies.

papers.title: Arbovirus circulation in Brazil: a scoping review protocol
papers.abstract: Arboviruses transmitted by Aedes species—predominantly Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus—represent a major public health challenge in Brazil. The co-circulation, re-emergence, and recurring epidemics of Dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), alongside the potential re-urbanization risk of Yellow Fever virus (YFV) over recent decades, have imposed severe health, social, and economic burdens across diverse geographic regions. Despite extensive epidemiological surveillance and research, literature remains fragmented regarding local variations in infection frequency, population susceptibility, diagnostic approaches, and regional disease burdens. A systematic mapping of published evidence—specifically focusing on human infection and exposure evidenced by laboratory detection methods (molecular, serological, or viral isolation)—is necessary to synthesize current knowledge, delineate spatial-temporal patterns, and identify critical evidence gaps in Aedes-borne arboviral research across Brazilian urban and peri-urban environments.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the fragmented literature necessitates a systematic mapping to better understand the spatial and temporal dynamics of Dengue virus and other Aedes-borne arboviruses in Brazil. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决对巴西伊蚊(尤其是 登革病毒)传播的虫媒病毒相关的感染频率、人群易感性、诊断方法和区域疾病负担的当地差异的零碎理解。这项研究的动机是这些病毒带来的重大公共卫生挑战,这些病毒给不同地理区域造成了严重的健康、社会和经济负担。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该范围审查协议概述了已发表证据的系统图谱,重点关注人类感染和接触 登革病毒 和其他伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒,特别是在巴西城市和城郊环境中。该研究跨越近几十年来,包括 登革病毒、寨卡病毒、基孔肯雅病毒的共同传播、重新出现和反复流行以及黄热病病毒潜在的再城市化风险的数据。
elements_zh.methods: 该审查将系统地绘制已发表的证据,特别关注通过分子、血清学或病毒分离技术等​​实验室检测方法证明的人类感染和暴露。该研究将综合现有知识,描绘时空模式,并确定巴西城市和城郊环境中伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒研究中的关键证据差距。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究报告称,关于巴西 登革病毒 和其他伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒相关的感染频率、人群易感性、诊断方法和区域疾病负担的当地差异,文献仍然支离破碎。它强调需要全面综合当前的知识来弥补这些差距。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,零碎的文献需要进行系统绘图,以更好地了解巴西 登革病毒 和其他伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒的空间和时间动态。这种方法的新颖之处在于它侧重于综合当前知识并确定关键证据差距。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为有针对性的 监测、改进的诊断策略和更有效的公共卫生干预措施提供信息,以减轻巴西 监测 和其他伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒的影响。他们还强调了解决疾病负担和感染模式的区域差异的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于范围审查方案,不提供原始结果。证据仅是抽象的,由于缺乏详细数据和审查的探索性,研究结果的可信度较低。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该范围审查协议概述了已发表证据的系统图谱,重点关注人类感染和接触 登革病毒 和其他伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒,特别是在巴西城市和城郊环境中。该研究跨越近几十年来,包括 登革病毒、寨卡病毒、基孔肯雅病毒的共同传播、重新出现和反复流行以及黄热病病毒潜在的再城市化风险的数据。
analysis_zh.methods: 该审查将系统地绘制已发表的证据,特别关注通过分子、血清学或病毒分离技术等​​实验室检测方法证明的人类感染和暴露。该研究将综合现有知识,描绘时空模式,并确定巴西城市和城郊环境中伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒研究中的关键证据差距。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究报告称,关于巴西 登革病毒 和其他伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒相关的感染频率、人群易感性、诊断方法和区域疾病负担的当地差异,文献仍然支离破碎。它强调需要全面综合当前的知识来弥补这些差距。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,零碎的文献需要进行系统绘图,以更好地了解巴西 登革病毒 和其他伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒的空间和时间动态。这种方法的新颖之处在于它侧重于综合当前知识并确定关键证据差距。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为有针对性的 监测、改进的诊断策略和更有效的公共卫生干预措施提供信息,以减轻巴西 监测 和其他伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒的影响。他们还强调了解决疾病负担和感染模式的区域差异的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于范围审查方案,不提供原始结果。证据仅是抽象的,由于缺乏详细数据和审查的探索性,研究结果的可信度较低。

papers.title: A dengue sob uma perspectiva epidemiológica e sociodemográfica: uma análise sobre o estado de Minas Gerais
papers.abstract: O contexto epidemiológico da dengue no Brasil caracteriza-se por oscilações entre períodos endêmicos e surtos epidêmicos, representando um desafio contínuo à saúde pública. Este estudo tem como objetivo geral analisar o perfil epidemiológico e sociodemográfico da dengue no estado de Minas Gerais, com ênfase no município de Uberlândia, a partir de evidências da literatura científica recente. Trata-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de caráter descritivo e exploratório, realizada em bases de dados nacionais e internacionais. Os resultados indicam elevada incidência da doença em determinados períodos do ano, forte associação com fatores socioambientais, desigualdades regionais e impacto significativo sobre o Sistema Único de Saúde. Conclui-se que a dengue permanece como um importante problema de saúde pública em Minas Gerais, exigindo estratégias integradas de vigilância epidemiológica, controle vetorial e ações intersetoriais.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a descriptive and exploratory bibliographic research conducted using national and international databases to analyze the epidemiological and sociodemographic profile of dengue in Minas Gerais, focusing on Uberlândia.
analysis.methods: The study employed a descriptive and exploratory bibliographic research approach, utilizing national and international databases to gather and analyze recent scientific evidence on dengue.
analysis.main_results: The results indicate a high incidence of dengue during certain periods of the year, a strong association with socio-environmental factors, regional inequalities, and a significant impact on the Unified Health System.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that dengue remains a significant public health problem in Minas Gerais, requiring integrated strategies for epidemiological surveillance, vector control, and intersectoral actions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for integrated surveillance and control strategies, highlighting the importance of addressing socio-environmental factors and regional inequalities to mitigate dengue's impact on the health system.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on bibliographic research, which may not capture all current or local data; however, the use of recent scientific evidence provides moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzes the epidemiological and sociodemographic profile of dengue in Minas Gerais, focusing on Uberlândia, through a descriptive and exploratory bibliographic review of recent scientific evidence. The research reveals high seasonal incidence of dengue, strong associations with socio-environmental factors, regional disparities, and significant impacts on the Unified Health System. The authors conclude that dengue remains a major public health challenge in the region, necessitating integrated approaches to surveillance, vector control, and intersectoral interventions. While the study's bibliographic nature limits its scope, the use of current scientific evidence provides moderate confidence in its conclusions and recommendations for addressing dengue's multifaceted challenges.

analysis_zh.methods: 该研究采用描述性和探索性的文献研究方法,利用国家和国际数据库收集和分析有关登革热的最新科学证据。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果表明,在一年中的某些时段,登革热的 发病率 较高,与社会环境因素、区域不平等密切相关,并对统一卫生系统产生重大影响。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,登革热仍然是米纳斯吉拉斯州的一个重大公共卫生问题,需要采取流行病学 监测、媒介 控制和跨部门行动的综合策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明需要采取综合的 监测 和控制策略,强调解决社会环境因素和区域不平等以减轻登革热对卫生系统影响的重要性。

papers.title: Priming and boosting the investigator pipeline for patient-oriented arboviral research
papers.abstract: This project is anchored in Dr. Matthew Collins’ sustained and growing career as a leader in translational arbovirology research and clinical work in Infectious Diseases and Travel Medicine, with the work proposed here growing out of an ongoing clinical trial designed to better understand protective immunity to dengue virus. As an Associate Professor in the Division of Infectious Diseases in the Emory University School of Medicine, he has been involved in patient-oriented research (POR) since his undergraduate experiences in the Vascular Biology Center at the Medical College of Georgia, a public institution charged with improving health outcomes for patients in Georgia. Ultimately pursuing an MD, PhD out of an interest and motivation to realize improved patient outcomes via rigorous discovery science, Collins developed ardent interest in tropical and emerging diseases, particularly vector-borne diseases, which represent a solvable global health problem that imposes a massive disease burden on human populations. This project will focus on a group of closely related viruses called flaviviruses – which includes dengue, Zika, yellow fever, and West Nile – while addressing a fundament gap in knowledge for many viruses: Does a combination of different exposures confer better immunity to a given virus? Leveraging a unique set of human samples, tools, and reagents, we will examine the breadth of flavivirus immunity generated by sequential vaccination with different dengue vaccines and assess how dengue infection impacts the strength and durability of protective immunity to yellow fever. Data generated in this study will have direct implications for ongoing product development as well as public health policy for existing approaches to preventing flavivirus infections. To accomplish the scientific goals of this project and his greater career goals, Dr. Collins has established a comprehensive career development plan that includes connection to a team of advisors, mentors, and collaborators and a focused set of knowledge (vaccinology), skills (biostatistics and trial design) and leadership (team science, academic career development and mentorship) building and training activities. These endeavors are largely accomplished via existing resources available at Emory University and include Clinical Research Bootcamp (Emory), a Vaccinology symposium (Keystone), ADVAC (Advanced course in vaccinology (U of Geneva)), and COMPASS (Career Optimization and Mentoring Program for Academic Success and Support, Emory School of Medicine). Finally, this proposal creates rich opportunities to recruit and mentor trainees in POR. Collins’ commitment to POR has been matched by a strong record of NIH and foundational funding and mentorship. His portfolio of mentees includes undergraduates, masters and doctoral students, medical residents and fellows, and postdocs. This proposal increases Dr. Collins’ abilities and effort in cultivating the next generation of POR investigators. The environment at Emory University affords a deep pool of talented mentees who will benefit from opportunities in team science, interdisciplinary arbovirology, and robust training in experimental design, advanced analyses, and science communication via projects that substantially contribute to ongoing efforts to improve human health and diminish arboviral disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aims to address a fundamental gap in understanding whether a combination of different exposures enhances immunity to dengue virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is an ongoing clinical trial designed to better understand protective immunity to dengue virus, involving human samples and focusing on sequential vaccination with different dengue vaccines.
analysis.methods: The methods include leveraging a unique set of human samples, tools, and reagents to examine the breadth of flavivirus immunity generated by sequential vaccination and assess the impact of dengue infection on yellow fever immunity.
analysis.main_results: The study directly observes the breadth of flavivirus immunity generated by sequential vaccination with different dengue vaccines and evaluates how dengue infection affects the strength and durability of protective immunity to yellow fever.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the findings will contribute to understanding the immune responses to dengue and related flaviviruses, offering novel insights into the potential benefits of combined exposures.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform ongoing product development and public health policy for preventing flavivirus infections, particularly dengue and yellow fever.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on an ongoing clinical trial, which may have limitations in generalizability and control, but the study's design and focus on dengue virus provide a moderate level of confidence in its conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores whether sequential vaccination with different dengue vaccines enhances immunity to dengue virus and how dengue infection affects protective immunity to yellow fever. The research is grounded in an ongoing clinical trial and leverages unique human samples to examine immune responses. The findings aim to improve understanding of flavivirus immunity and inform vaccine development and public health strategies. While the study provides valuable insights, its reliance on an ongoing trial may limit generalizability, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项正在进行的临床试验,旨在更好地了解对 登革病毒 的保护性免疫力,涉及人体样本,并重点关注不同登革热 疫苗 的连续 疫苗接种。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法包括利用一组独特的人类样本、工具和试剂来检查连续 疫苗接种 产生的黄病毒免疫的广度,并评估登革热感染对黄热病免疫的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究直接观察了连续疫苗接种与不同登革热疫苗产生的黄病毒免疫的广度,并评估登革热感染如何影响黄热病保护性免疫的强度和持久性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,这些发现将有助于了解 免疫应答 对登革热和相关黄病毒的影响,为联合暴露的潜在益处提供新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为正在进行的预防黄病毒感染(特别是登革热和黄热病)的产品开发和公共卫生政策提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该证据基于正在进行的临床试验,该试验可能在普遍性和控制方面存在局限性,但该研究的设计和对 登革病毒 的关注为其结论提供了中等程度的可信度。

papers.abstract_zh: 该项目以 Matthew Collins 博士作为传染病和旅行医学转化虫媒病毒学研究和临床工作领导者持续不断发展的职业生涯为基础,这里提出的工作源于一项正在进行的临床试验,旨在更好地了解 登革病毒 的保护性免疫。作为埃默里大学医学院传染病系的副教授,自乔治亚医学院血管生物学中心(一家负责改善乔治亚州患者健康结果的公共机构)本科学习起,他就一直参与以患者为导向的研究 (POR)。最终,柯林斯出于通过严格的发现科学来改善患者治疗效果的兴趣和动机,攻读了医学博士、博士学位,他对热带和新出现的疾病,特别是 媒介 传播的疾病产生了浓厚的兴趣,这些疾病代表了一个可解决的全球健康问题,给人类带来了巨大的疾病负担。该项目将重点关注一组密切相关的黄病毒病毒(包括登革热、寨卡病毒、黄热病和西尼罗河病毒),同时解决许多病毒的基本知识空白:不同暴露的组合是否会对特定病毒产生更好的免疫力?利用一套独特的人体样本、工具和试剂,我们将检查连续 疫苗接种 与不同登革热 疫苗 产生的黄病毒免疫的广度,并评估登革热感染如何影响黄热病保护性免疫的强度和持久性。这项研究产生的数据将对正在进行的产品开发以及预防黄病毒感染的现有方法的公共卫生政策产生直接影响。为了实现该项目的科学目标和他更大的职业目标,柯林斯博士制定了全面的职业发展计划,其中包括与顾问、导师和合作者团队的联系以及一系列重点知识(疫苗学)、技能(生物统计学和试验设计)和领导力(团队科学、学术职业发展和指导)建设和培训活动。这些努力主要是通过埃默里大学的现有资源完成的,包括临床研究训练营(埃默里)、疫苗学研讨会(Keystone)、ADVAC(疫苗学高级课程(日内瓦大学))和 COMPASS(埃默里医学院职业优化和学术成功与支持辅导计划)。最后,该提案为招募和指导 POR 学员创造了丰富的机会。柯林斯对 POR 的承诺与 NIH 的良好记录以及基金会的资助和指导相匹配。他的学员包括本科生、硕士生和博士生、住院医师和研究员以及博士后。该提案增加了 Collins 博士培养下一代 POR 研究人员的能力和努力。埃默里大学的环境为大量才华横溢的学员提供了机会,他们将受益于团队科学、跨学科虫媒病毒学的机会,以及通过项目进行的实验设计、高级分析和科学传播方面的强有力的培训,这些项目对改善人类健康和减少虫媒病毒疾病的持续努力做出了重大贡献。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决理解不同暴露组合是否可以增强对 登革病毒 免疫力的根本差距。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项正在进行的临床试验,旨在更好地了解对 登革病毒 的保护性免疫力,涉及人体样本,并重点关注不同登革热 疫苗 的连续 疫苗接种。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些方法包括利用一组独特的人类样本、工具和试剂来检查连续 疫苗接种 产生的黄病毒免疫的广度,并评估登革热感染对黄热病免疫的影响。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究直接观察了连续疫苗接种与不同登革热疫苗产生的黄病毒免疫的广度,并评估登革热感染如何影响黄热病保护性免疫的强度和持久性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,这些发现将有助于了解 免疫应答 对登革热和相关黄病毒的影响,为联合暴露的潜在益处提供新的见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为正在进行的预防黄病毒感染(特别是登革热和黄热病)的产品开发和公共卫生政策提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该证据基于正在进行的临床试验,该试验可能在普遍性和控制方面存在局限性,但该研究的设计和对 登革病毒 的关注为其结论提供了中等程度的可信度。

papers.title: Analysis of Cell Populations from Arbovirus-Infected Tissues by Flow Cytometry.
papers.abstract: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

papers.title_zh: 通过流式细胞术分析虫媒病毒感染组织的细胞群。
papers.source_body_en: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

papers.title: Development of a Single Thermal Cycling Multiplex RT-qPCR Assay for Rapid Arbovirus Detection
papers.abstract: Background: The co-circulation of multiple arboviruses with similar clinical presentations poses a significant challenge for public health surveillance. This study aimed to develop and clinically validate a novel multiplex RT-qPCR assay for the simultaneous detection of five arboviruses in three reactions. Methods: A diagnostic accuracy study was conducted in Salvador, Brazil. Evaluation was performed using 254 prospective serum samples and 34 archived positive samples. The primers and probes for the assay were designed in silico, all targeting highly conserved regions of Dengue (DENV), Zika (ZIKV), Chikungunya (CHIKV), Oropouche (OROV), and West Nile (WNV) viruses. The protocol was optimized in three reactions with a single thermal cycle, comprising a tetraplex reaction (DENV, CHIKV, ZIKV, and hRNAseP, an endogenous control) and two singleplex reactions (OROV and WNV). Results: In prospective analysis, the assay identified 45 DENV, 3 CHIKV, and 9 OROV-positive cases. Diagnostic accuracy for DENV and CHIKV was 96% (95% CI: 93.3–98.0%), successfully detecting four DENV cases missed by the reference standard. Furthermore, incorporating OROV enabled the identification of nine cases that conventional triplex protocols would have overlooked. Conclusion: This single-cycling multiplex RT-qPCR assay enhances epidemiological surveillance by expanding detection beyond traditional triplex targets to include OROV and WNV. This operational optimization reduces turnaround times and prevents the underdiagnosis of emerging arboviruses, serving as a robust diagnostic tool for endemic regions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 具有相似临床表现的多种虫媒病毒的共同循环对公共卫生提出了重大挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在巴西萨尔瓦多进行了一项诊断准确性研究。使用 254 份前瞻性血清样本和 34 份存档的阳性样本进行评估。
elements_zh.methods: 该检测的引物和探针均通过计算机设计,均针对登革热 (DENV)、寨卡 (ZIKV)、基孔肯雅 (CHIKV)、奥罗普切 (OROV) 和西尼罗河 (WNV) 病毒的高度保守区域。该方案在单个热循环的三个反应中进行了优化,包括一个四重反应(DENV、CHIKV、ZIKV 和 hRNAseP,内源性对照)和两个单重反应(OROV 和 WNV)。
elements_zh.main_results: 在前瞻性分析中,该检测确定了 45 例 DENV、3 例 CHIKV 和 9 例 OROV 阳性病例。DENV 和 CHIKV 的诊断准确率为 96%(95% CI:93.3-98.0%),成功检出参考标准漏检的 4 例 DENV 病例。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这种单循环多重 RT-qPCR 检测将检测范围扩展到传统三重靶标之外,包括 OROV 和 WNV,从而增强了流行病学 监测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这种操作优化缩短了周转时间,并防止对新兴虫媒病毒的诊断不足,成为流行地区的强大诊断工具。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告局限性或证据强度。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:具有相似临床表现的多种虫媒病毒的共同循环对公共卫生提出了重大挑战 监测。本研究旨在开发并临床验证一种新型多重 RT-qPCR 检测方法,用于在三个反应中同时检测五种虫媒病毒。方法:在巴西萨尔瓦多进行了一项诊断准确性研究。使用 254 份前瞻性血清样本和 34 份存档的阳性样本进行评估。该检测的引物和探针均通过计算机设计,均针对登革热 (DENV)、寨卡 (ZIKV)、基孔肯雅 (CHIKV)、奥罗普切 (OROV) 和西尼罗河 (WNV) 病毒的高度保守区域。该方案在单个热循环的三个反应中进行了优化,包括一个四重反应(DENV、CHIKV、ZIKV 和 hRNAseP,内源性对照)和两个单重反应(OROV 和 WNV)。结果:在前瞻性分析中,该检测确定了 45 例 DENV、3 例 CHIKV 和 9 例 OROV 阳性病例。DENV 和 CHIKV 的诊断准确率为 96%(95% CI:93.3-98.0%),成功检出参考标准漏检的 4 例 DENV 病例。此外,结合 OROV 可以识别传统三重协议可能忽略的九种情况。结论:这种单循环多重 RT-qPCR 检测将检测范围扩展到传统三重靶标之外,包括 OROV 和 WNV,从而增强了流行病学 监测。这种操作优化缩短了周转时间,并防止对新兴虫媒病毒的诊断不足,成为流行地区的强大诊断工具。
