supplementary_news.content: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home Culture – Society Medical Dengue fever: Do not be complacent when the fever subsides, even in young, healthy individuals. With the southern region accounting for 73.1% of all dengue fever cases nationwide, experts warn that anyone can develop severe symptoms, including young, healthy individuals. Báo Nhân dân•02/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 Dr. Truong Huu Khanh emphasized that one should not be complacent when contracting dengue fever. (Photo: HCDC) Identifying high-risk groups At the seminar "Who is at risk of developing severe complications from dengue fever?" organized by the Ho Chi Minh City Center for Disease Control (HCDC) in collaboration with Takeda Vietnam Pharmaceutical Company Limited, experts analyzed in detail why these groups are more susceptible to dangerous complications. According to Dr. Than Ha Ngoc The, President of the Vietnam Palliative Care Medicine Association and Vice President of the Ho Chi Minh City Geriatrics Association, in the elderly, the aging process is accompanied by a decline in immune function and reduced physiological reserves, while underlying conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or chronic kidney disease can make the treatment of Dengue fever more complicated. Khám phá thêm Tìm hiểu lịch sử Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch Khám phá ĐNA Đọc Tin Tức tin Tin Tức Tra cứu tài liệu DU LỊCH Du lịch Làm dịch vụ SEO Notably, dengue fever in the elderly often presents with atypical symptoms. Instead of high fever or noticeable aches and pains, patients may only experience restlessness, lethargy, or confusion. These signs are easily overlooked or mistaken for common health problems associated with old age. Regarding children, Dr. Truong Huu Khanh - former Head of the Infectious Diseases and Neurology Department, Children's Hospital 1 (Ho Chi Minh City) - noted particular concern for high-risk groups including children under 1 year old, overweight or obese children, or those with underlying medical conditions. Especially in infants, symptoms are often unclear, and the sudden progression of the disease when it worsens is very difficult to predict. In older children, being overweight or obese can also increase the risk of developing severe, life-threatening complications such as dengue hemorrhagic shock. due to plasma leakage. Dr. Than Ha Ngoc The (left) said that fluid replacement in the elderly needs to be carefully assessed and monitored, as both fluid deficiency and fluid overload can complicate the patient's condition. Pregnant women also need to be closely monitored for dengue fever because the disease can be associated with complications in both mother and fetus, including postpartum hemorrhage, premature birth, and low birth weight. During pregnancy, women should prioritize mosquito bite prevention measures and discuss appropriate prevention plans with healthcare professionals before, during, and after pregnancy. You may also like However, dengue fever is not just a problem for high-risk groups. Even young, healthy people can develop severe symptoms, even death. Recently, the Ho Chi Minh City Hospital for Tropical Diseases admitted two patients, aged 16 and 21, in critical condition: one case required high-tech treatment such as ECMO for over a month at a cost of nearly 1 billion VND, while the other required continuous hemodialysis for 45 days. On September 8th, the hospital also recorded a death in a 20-year-old patient due to severe dengue fever. "Doctors never dare to make assumptions about whether one case will be mild or another will be severe. All patients have the potential to become seriously ill," emphasized Dr. Truong Huu Khanh. The consequences of a severe case of dengue fever extend beyond health and medical expenses; it can lead to missed school or work days, lost income, and significant psychological stress for the patient, their family, and the medical team. The fever subsiding doesn't mean the danger is over. With some illnesses, the disease is considered cured once the fever subsides. However, with Dengue fever, the critical phase often occurs on days 3-7 of the illness, when the patient's fever may have already subsided. If not monitored and treated promptly, the disease can progress to severe complications such as Dengue hemorrhagic shock due to plasma leakage, severe bleeding, or severe organ damage: liver, kidney, heart, lung, or brain failure... Warning signs to watch out for include: restlessness, lethargy, drowsiness; severe and persistent abdominal pain, especially in the liver area; frequent vomiting; bleeding gums or nosebleeds; vomiting blood or bloody stools; unusually heavy menstruation; decreased urination (not urinating for more than 6 hours); cold hands and feet. According to Doctor Truong Huu Khanh, signs of fatigue in obese children are often difficult to recognize because they may still be alert and talkative. Therefore, parents should not be complacent but need to observe and inquire carefully. In older adults, the signs may be more subtle, such as lethargy, drowsiness, agitation, confusion, decreased urination, rapid breathing, or difficulty breathing. In particular, people taking beta-blockers (a group of medications commonly prescribed by doctors for cardiovascular diseases, hypertension, etc.) may not exhibit a rapid heart rate even in shock; therefore, one should not wait until a rapid heartbeat is detected to consider it a dangerous sign. When warning signs appear, especially in high-risk groups, patients should be taken immediately to the nearest medical facility instead of continuing to self-monitor at home. Experts recommend that each family should proactively prevent disease by implementing three layers of protection. You may also like Firstly, it is necessary to regularly eliminate mosquito larvae and prevent mosquito bites by removing stagnant water, cleaning up the living environment, and sleeping under a mosquito net, even during the day. Secondly, be vigilant if you have a fever. During peak season, elderly people or those with underlying health conditions should seek medical attention early if they experience fever and provide complete information about their underlying health conditions and medications they are currently taking so that the doctor can conduct a comprehensive assessment. In addition to mosquito control and proper disease monitoring, to help build active immunity against the Dengue virus, people should discuss Dengue fever vaccination with healthcare professionals to receive advice based on age and specific indications.
